items.title: The 143 best holiday gifts in 2026 – obsessively tested by the Guardian US
paragraphs: Nothing says holiday cheer quite like panic-browsing websites in pursuit of the perfect gift, toggling between 47 open tabs, eyes straining against your screen’s harsh blue light. But finding an item that elicits a squeal of delight from its recipient is one of the best parts of this time of year, when you have a little help.
So we’ve curated 143 presents to reclaim holiday shopping as a joyous activity.

We recruited seasoned writers and shopping experts to get into the holiday spirit early, vetting gifts across categories such as kitchen, home, tech and more. For months, we cooked, ate, traveled, hiked, ran, showered and slept with test products by our side. And we roped in our mothers, cats, dogs and the kids in our lives to make sure these gifts really work for the people (and pets!) they are meant for.

Our comprehensive list spans safe bets (who doesn’t like chocolate?) to niche recommendations (butter-shaped candle, anyone?). You’ll find a range of prices from a $6 cleaning cloth for a notoriously dirty laptop owner to a sophisticated trenchcoat for your stylish sister. Happy gifting.
Don’t see anything that catches your eye? Email us at thefilterus@theguardian.com for help finding a gift for your trickiest recipient.
Curated by Emily Farris and Karen Yuan. Farris has been writing about food and lifestyle and testing cooking gear for nearly 20 years.
Yuan covers food, kitchen gear and lifestyle for the Filter US. Her dream Christmas gift is a lifetime supply of cheesy ramen, and she has never turned down an invitation to hotpot.

I’m a sucker for a great-smelling hand soap. (I definitely snapped a picture of the label after my first pump of Aesop’s Resurrection.) If you know a home cook who’s equally enamored with luxe smells, add a bottle or three of Naomi’s hand scrub to your cart immediately. Specially formulated for the kitchen, it’s made with bread yeast enzymes to neutralize cooking odors and leaves behind sophisticated notes of bergamot and pepper that give off high-end hotel vibes. Emily Farris

These tiny French spoons get more use than any other utensils in my kitchen. Technically called demitasse spoons, they are the “teaspoons” of many European flatware sets, but they’re much, much smaller. My sons and I use them daily for yogurt, dessert, ice-cream and even most of our cereals. They’re perfect for espresso drinkers, homes with kids and anyone who just really loves small spoons (which inexplicably includes many neurodivergent people). They’re dishwasher-safe too! EF

I lost half of my kitchen knives in my divorce and instead of overthinking individual replacements, I opted for this trio from Material Kitchen. The chef’s knife, serrated knife and paring knife cover the needs of most home cooks – and after more than a year of near-daily use, the Japanese steel blades on all three are still sharp. It’s a great starter set or starting-over set, and it’s available with or without a magnetic knife stand. EF

Equal parts form and function, this minimalist dish drying mat is made of diatomaceous earth, which can absorb up to 150% of its weight in water – and shockingly quickly. I started using one a few years ago and I’m sold for life. This thing dries itself even more quickly than it dries dishes (yes, it’s very fun to watch), so I no longer worry about standing water or musty microfiber. I’d recommend it for kitchen aesthetes, but honestly anyone who hand-washes even just a few dishes will love it. It’s foldable for storage and travel too. EF

I wasn’t really a wine glass snob until I ended up with a single Zalto Denk’Art Universal Glass. Many sommeliers will tell you that Zalto makes the best wine glasses money can buy, but at nearly $80 a piece, my money can’t afford a full set – especially because the thin glass is extremely delicate and we all know how things go when the wine starts flowing. But Fable’s versatile wine glasses are a visual dupe for Zalto’s and they are much more affordable. While the lead-safe crystal isn’t quite as thin, it’s durable enough that multiple guests have knocked over or dropped mine, and in two years, I’ve lost only one. (The other three go in the dishwasher regularly.) EF

OK, fine! No one needs $52 “resting stones” for cooking utensils. But these satisfyingly hefty pebbles make my cooking so much more convenient and delightful. One stone lives beside the stove, ready to receive a sauce-slick tasting spoon or chopsticks. Another sits on my kitchen island, where I can pop a lime wedge or cracked egg shell on it. Because they don’t look like kitchen tools, they double as minimalist-looking decor when I’m not cooking. You could also use one as a tray for rings or keys. Karen Yuan

I once spotted this mug at a painfully cool cafe in Brooklyn, which was very validating for me, a not particularly cool person who nonetheless appreciates a nice trinket. The translucent amber glass has a honeyed glow that’s even lovelier in person, especially when the light catches it, and the mug’s angular square handle is surprisingly comfortable to hold. I am telling you, this set makes my everyday cup of Trader Joe’s tea taste like artisanal brew plucked from the loftiest tea fields in China. Gift it to your favorite coffee or tea drinker. KY

When I’m craving hotpot but it’s too cold to venture out to a restaurant, I’ll pull this bright red set from my shelf. The electric cooker heats up quickly and the pot is just the right size for one or two. If you judge the idea of “personal hotpot” the way one judges “personal pizza”, I am sorry for the lack of joy and whimsy in your life. This starter set comes with chili crisp samplers to make your own hotpot base, though you can also buy Fly By Jing’s premade base, which produces a savory, tongue-tingling broth with a satisfying kick of Sichuan peppercorn. Give it to a homebody who loves to cook, then wait for the hotpot dinner invite. Everyone wins! KY

These are dinner plates that make me want to invite people over just to have an excuse to use them. Their gently undulating rims give them a hand-molded look, but they are not just decorative; they offer a secure grip when I’m ferrying a stack of dishes to the sink or rinsing off a slippery plate. Made in Mexico from high-fired stoneware, they are pleasingly substantial, and the colors are warm and slightly retro. The brand also offers bread plates and salad plates. Tortuga Forma is a woman-owned small business founded just eight years ago, so you can use this chance to support an independent maker while upgrading someone’s dining table. KY

Kitschy food decor is everywhere now, and this one is a classic example. This $22 candle looks like a block of fancy French butter, right down to the gingham wrapper and “beurre salé” label. It’s actually made of soy wax and smells of jasmine, neroli and orange blossom, so it can act as anything from a dinner party curio to a kitchen candle that reduces odors. Give it to your most butter-obsessed friend. (It’s OK if that’s yourself.) KY
Curated by Richard Baguley, who has tested and written about consumer technology for more than 30 years. His favorite gift would be a good night’s sleep.

Is the weight of your worries keeping you awake? Adding more weight might help: the Bearaby Weighted Blanket feels like a giant cuddle and the ventilated faux knitted design means you will not get hot. It is oddly soothing while snoozing or watching TV, making it a great gift for someone you live with, just so you can use it, too. Richard Baguley

I may not be pregnant, but I am a terrible sleeper who grabs on to things while sleeping like a drowning man with a life-saver. Body pillows including the Buffy Wiggle Pillow offer something for me to grab on to in my night-time desperation and replace my knee pillow, while still leaving enough room in the bed for my long suffering wife. This is a perfect gift for anyone who struggles with sleep and wants to try new ways to improve it (pregnant or not). RB

When I was three years old, I insisted on sleeping with a spanner (translation to US English: wrench), perhaps because Warmies hadn’t been invented yet. Now I have upgraded to this adorable plush Capybara Warmie. Microwave it a minute and it gets cozy and warm, or stick it in the freezer for a cooling cuddle on a warm night. Unlike a spanner, it offers a subtle scent from the grain and lavender stuffing. RB

Have a family member who suffers from aches, cramps or excessively grumbly guts? This cute heater bottle might help: pop it into the microwave for a minute and it provides comfortable, soothing and safe heat that helps ease the aches, cramps and pains of modern life. It’s the perfect size for shoulders, tummies and feet that need soothing warmth. RB

I love my dog Jasper, but he snores like a badly oiled diesel engine. The Alpine Silence are the best earplugs I have found for those nights when you just want him – or the person sleeping next to you – to stop. The V-shaped handle makes them easy to pop in, take out, and even holds them in place. They are easier to carry than earbuds, don’t need charging and cost a lot less if your dog decides they look like a tasty treat. RB

Sheets are the kind of gift that no one really thinks about giving, but their recipients will be touched (and happy) to receive. They are an essential component for a good night’s sleep, and these are the best. The 280-count percale cotton is smooth on the skin, hard-wearing and provides a little touch of luxury as you doze off. RB

Satin pillowcases help keep your skin smooth and your hair undamaged. This one is available in a Galactic Empire or Rebel Alliance theme, depending on your political orientation to the Force. Honestly though, they missed a trick by not doing a pillow with the empire on one side and the rebellion on the other and marketing it with a joke about turning to the cool, dark side … RB

The world is a noisy place when you are trying to nap and AirPods will jab you in the ear when you roll over. The Sleepcore A20 earbuds have a flat design that fits right inside your ears, plus a soft exterior and swappable ear tips that make for excellent sound blocking and all-night comfort. If your special someone spends their evenings doomscrolling with the sound on, slip these in their stocking and give yourself the gift of silence – the earbuds offer a 10-hour battery life when playing audiobooks from your phone and they come with a handy charging case. Alternatively, give them as a present to yourself to block the sounds of constant doom. RB

People spend more time in pyjamas than most clothes, so a decent set is an investment in the care and comfort of those you love. These Cozy Earth Bamboo pyjamas are wonderfully cozy, with a flexible fit and a wonderful feeling of smooth luxury. The breathable bamboo fabric also keeps things cool on a warm night. RB

Sleep rituals can help you wind down and relax after a head-spinning day. The Twilight gift set from Lush will help anyone develop this kind of routine. I’m normally skeptical of such potions, but I found the Sleepy shower gel and body lotion to be very effective: the lavender scent genuinely helps me to put the day behind and sleep better. RB

Curated by Jon Chan, who has been writing about home, outdoor and tech products since 2012. His favorite Christmas gift was a tie covered in crabs. No matter how dire the situation, a crab shuffle dance will make life a little better.

If you know someone who desperately needs a spa day but can never find the time, bring the spa to them. The Parachute Organic Super Plush towels are some of the best we have ever tested. Made of thick, squishy organic Turkish cotton, Parachute’s towels are soft from edge to edge, giving you a sense of coziness that other towel brands struggle to match. Yes, these towels are more expensive than those you will find at a big box store, but they are an attainable luxury – and a really good gift. Jon Chan

Bubble and faux-fur blankets such as the Lola got really trendy on social media, but they can be really expensive. The Bubble Blanket from Bedsure, made from the same Oeko-Tex standard 100-certified materials, is a better bet at a third of the price. Our testing found it’s warm and amazingly soft, like being wrapped in a teddy bear’s hug. JC

Give your household the gift of a permanent truce from the thermostat wars: a good space heater, specifically this one from Honeywell. Its HeatPhase Timer sets it apart from the competition: when activated, it lowers the power (and temperature) every 30 minutes until it hits the lowest tier and shuts off. You’ll feel cozy as you drift off to sleep and will not wake up a sweaty mess a few hours later. JC

A good throw pillow will inject color, energy and life into an otherwise ho-hum space. Piecework, a company best known for its intricate puzzles, has branched out into home goods, and these pillows are just as delightful as its mainstays. The cases are screen printed on to sturdy cotton, so the colors will stay bold, and the styles range from floral to geometric. They’re cheerful without being too maximalist, and you can find one to match any aesthetic. JC

As colder weather rolls in, so does the flu, flaky skin and dry air – bringing plenty of reasons to get a humidifier. The Levoit Classic 300S is small enough to fit on a desk or bedside table with a tank large enough to run for 16 hours straight on the highest setting. It’s easily refilled from the top, so you are not giving the gift of extra work and the control panel is dimmable and can act like a nightlight. JC

If the beach-goer in your life is sick of lugging a hard-sided cooler full of seltzer, give them (and their back) something that will help. MagPack’s backpack soft cooler has a magnetic lock and frame that helps ensure what’s inside doesn’t get crushed and will not leak out. And when it is sealed and packed with ice, it keeps drinks cold all day and through the night. JC

The best work gloves balance dexterity with protection. We found that Carhartt’s A518 gloves fit that bill. Double-stitched cowhide pads cover the fingertips, palm, part of the wrist and the knuckles, so all your bits are covered – and they’re flexible enough to allow you to open pocket knives and change drill bits with ease. Stuff these in a stocking for someone who is always working on a project in their garage or garden. JC

Know someone who is on the fence about bathrobes? They need a bath sheet – something that provides the coverage of a luxury robe with the ease of storage like a regular towel. American Linen has a great bath sheet that is 40in x 80in of plush Turkish cotton. JC

Between wildfire smoke and pollution, air quality is a rising concern. If you are interested in giving the gift of clean air to a loved one, this Shark air purifier is one of the best I have tested, with a Hepa and carbon filter that can last up to five years. JC

For someone who is constantly battling dust bunnies and pet hair, a robot vacuum can help win the war. The Eufy 11S Max is great entry-level model to give to someone curious about robot vacs, but unsure if they will jive well with their floor plan. At just under 3in tall, this short king can squeeze under a lot of furniture and the powerful motor is great at removing dust and debris. JC

Curated by Tim Stevens. Stevens travels 200,000 miles a year and has covered travel gear, consumer technology and everything in between since 1996. His favorite Christmas gift was a Sega CD in 1992, and he considers himself lucky to have survived the console wars.

This super-simple solution to keeping a laptop display pristine makes for a great stocking stuffer. Laid over a laptop’s keys when closed, it protects the display from micro-abrasions while also providing a handy cloth to wipe away any dust. Perfect for the traveling perfectionist in your life. Tim Stevens

Socks are perhaps not the most exciting of gifts, compression socks doubly so, but deep-vein thrombosis is nothing to mess with. Compression is a great and simple way to minimize the risk. I have had a pair of these Wanderlust socks for five years now. They are still comfortable and look like new, perfect for the frequent-flying buy-it-for-lifer in your family circle. TS

I have found myself traveling with paper books again lately, partly because I enjoy the experience and partly because it is a lot less expensive to forget a book than a Kindle. Hotels rarely have good bedside reading lights and this tiny, long-lasting and rechargeable option is the best gift I have given myself so that I can read in bed. Any globe-trotting reader in your life will be similarly appreciative. TS

While it is not the most exciting thing on this list, I’m convinced this is the perfect bag for your carry-on liquid allotment. It’s sort of like a cross between a regular Ziploc bag and a storage container, but thick and stretchy enough to conform to whatever you are packing. It will not pop open and it even stands up, making it easy to access everything inside. It’s a great gift for any traveler looking to cut down on single-use plastic bags. TS

Anker has upped its charging game again, integrating a high-power USB-C charger and universal travel adapter into one. With four USB ports (three USB-C and one -A), it will charge everything from smartwatches to laptops and do it anywhere in the world. It is my new travel companion and a perfect gift for that friend who is always borrowing your charger. TS

Long hours on cramped airplanes do a number on your back. Yoga is a huge part of how I keep things limber, but yoga without a mat is a real challenge. These gloves and booties are like tiny yoga mats you can wear, surprisingly functional yet small enough to be easily packable. I was skeptical at first, but I bring these on every trip. Any yoga fan in your life will too. TS

Most hotels still don’t put enough outlets in convenient places. This cable is long enough to free you to work wherever you want in your room, but not so huge that it will take up half your bag. If you know a frequent traveler who spends lots of time working in hotel rooms, this gift will keep them from being tethered to the wall. TS

Smart packing means minimizing liquids, but saving your skin should take priority. This Dr Jart+ stick provides SPF 40 protection, goes on easily, smells nice and doesn’t need to fit in your little bag of liquids. It is ideal for anyone who needs some extra sun protection on the go, especially men who are not too keen on the whole daily moisturizing routine. TS

Speaking of gifts for men who don’t want any more liquids in their carry-on, a bar of shaving soap will surely be well received. This bar from Gentleman Jon smells great, lathers well and should last for at least a year of regular shaving. TS

Apple’s AirTags are button-sized pucks that wirelessly connect to Apple devices within Bluetooth range to report their approximate location. Put one in your bag, and you will always know where it is. If you have a forgetful friend or someone whose checked bags tend to disappear, they make a great gift. TS

Curated by Maria Ricapito, who has covered beauty and wellness long enough to see every makeup trend come around at least thrice. This Christmas, if someone gave her one of those Ocura Life Plasma Pens to remove random bits, bumps and skin tags, she would definitely try it out and let you know if it works.

I cannot wait to tell my nephews that I put some Cat Crap in their stockings. This would be great for a snarky and sporty teen (or adult). It’s a functional, basic and un-tinted lip balm with a vanilla mint flavor and SPF 15 from a company that makes a defogger for sports goggles. You may also find it by the register at your local hiking/climbing/biking/skiing shop. Maria Ricapito

When my friend with long, wavy hair bought me my first WetBrush, she told me that it would be life-changing. Eight years later, I agree – it is nice to brush out my curly, frizz-prone wet locks without pulling out a clump of strands every time. This version is tiny but mighty; it is small enough to tuck into a gym or travel bag. I prefer the open design versus the traditional cushiony paddle type because it dries quickly. Give it to someone who has been using the same ratty Goody brush since the early 2000s. MR

This travel-friendly set uses African botanicals to fight hyperpigmentation (AKA dark spots) and hydrate skin. The recently released line was developed by Sabrina and Idris Elba, in partnership with Farm Africa. It makes a lovely gift for the skincare-obsessive always looking for the next and newest thing. MR

For those of us who lack fireplaces, as I did for years living in New York City, this candle is the next best thing. Made in Bushwick, Brooklyn, DS & Durga’s scent really fits the brief – a heady mix of cedar, pine, oak and birch notes in a soy wax candle with amber-hued glass that does genuinely smell like a roaring, crackling fire. MR

Gnarly feet happen, especially in overheated, dry winter air. I have certainly tried every cream, lotion or salve that is meant to give you baby-soft soles. Those help, but this tool provides the finishing touch. It is like taking a (gentle) electric sander to your heels and toes – and is so much safer than aggressive cheese-grater foot files or, God forbid, the bloody callus shavers that are banned in salons in some states. Give it to someone who prides themselves on their DIY pedicures. MR

I have had my Dyson blowdryer for several years with no signs of needing to replace it. I like it for the results: quicker drying and lots of adjustable levels of heat and blowage, plus less-fried hair. But as time and tech have moved on, the brand’s latest versions have new features such as “pause detect mode”, “attachment learning” and “scalp protect mode”. This model comes with the aforementioned bells and whistles as well as five magnetic attachments for different styling needs (to smooth flyaways, pouf up curls, concentrate air flow and detangle). Give this to someone whose janky old drugstore hairdryer is on the fritz – it’s worth it. MR

Introduce your favorite perfume-lover to Leland Francis, a brand founded by Dillon Peñas, an Oklahoma-native makeup artist, with this rollerball trio. It offers an oil-based, alcohol-free combo in three personalities: El Santo (citrus and wood), La Reina (rose and herb) and Stoner (smoke and leather). The brand is gender-inclusive, so each fragrance is unisex and the products are made in small batches and packaged with recyclable materials. The trio can also be bought separately as an eau de parfum or scented candle. MR

Nearly everyone you know probably has some kind of retainer, aligner or night guard that could use a good (and quick) cleaning. The fizzy tablets are fine, but you can’t live with others and leave your retainer soaking by your sink. Bad things happen: imagine your night guard falling off the sink edge into the toilet (and the guilty party just … putting it back). This gadget works by creating high-frequency ultrasonic waves that create bubbles to gently break down the gunge. Upgrade someone’s oral care – you may even be able to pay for it with your HSA account! MR

The colorful packaging and fruity flavors make this a stocking stuffer that is sure to impress anyone who is a tween (or tween at heart). Starface is the brand that made pimple patches an accessory for the gen Z set, but the lip balm also won the best flavored balm in our roundup. Choose a bundle of like-minded flavors or pick from the full list. (Purists, never fear: there’s an unscented version.) The goop itself is a soothing, hydrating mix of shea butter, cocoa butter and coconut oil that is vegan, cruelty-free and safe for sensitive skin. MR

When I want to air-dry my hair without dripping water on to my shoulders, I pop on one of these. These scrunchies are made from a microfiber towel material that supposedly speeds drying time and looks nice enough for the beach or poolside. The brand uses almost 100% sustainable, eco-friendly and recycled materials and partners with 4Ocean to remove plastics from the sea. It is a great gift for anyone with a dedicated air-drying hair regimen or anyone who wants the ease of a towel without wearing one in public. MR

I love these pencils for their ability to make even the most inelegant application look intentional. You don’t need to blend; the thick rounded pencil is a multitasker, and can do anything from a barely noticeable line to full-on smokey eye glam. It comes in a range of 16 shades, including Iced Latte (a pinkish-tan) or Matcha (lime green shimmer that is not too try-hard). And at just $6 each, they are a great stocking stuffer for anyone who watches makeup tutorials or wants to try out colorful eye looks. MR

Silk bonnets and satin pillowcases are great for waking up with smoother morning hair – but don’t overlook the humble scrunchie. Kitsch’s satin version is Oeko-Tex certified and the brand’s dedication to sustainability makes this an easy buy for anyone with hair longer than a kicky little bob. MR

This Japanese skin ritual in a very giftable bamboo box aims to fix dryness and uneven texture. The Silk Rice makeup-removing cleansing oil, Citrus Glow vitamin C and hyaluronic acid serum, Matcha Boost eye serum and Mochi Mochi luminous plumping moisturizer contain traditional Japanese ingredients including shiso (antioxidant and rich in fatty acids) and matcha extract (helps shield against sun damage), plus vitamin C to brighten skin. It is an easy gift for skincare fanatics looking to expand their horizons beyond Tatcha, another popular Japanese skincare brand. MR

This funky-looking portable system is not just a keychain – it is a detachable cube filled with solid fragrance. It is great for travel and also makes for a nice accessory: when assembled, the cube looks functional and unisex, like a sporty bag charm. The scents themselves are meant to be unisex – Heroic Dose is a herbaceous aromatic with a whiff of salt air and Altered States is a woody scent with spicy nutmeg, cardamom and tonka. This will be an unexpected gift for a perfume lover’s collection – or just a nice treat for yourself. MR

Curated by Lauren Gould. She has covered style for the Filter US for the past year, from bravely asking New Yorkers about their outfits to interviewing stylists. Her favorite Christmas gift was a Tiffany & Co silver necklace with her initials, which made her feel like Blair Waldorf from Gossip Girl.

This purse’s appearance will deceive you – it looks far more expensive than its $98 price tag. I use the red version to hold my cards, work ID, makeup, Kindle and of course, my daily GoMacro bar. It adds a fun pop of color to any outfit, and I love to style it with an all-black ensemble or a simple sweater. My one quibble is small but mighty: the removable drawstring pouch tends to crinkle up in the purse, which is quite annoying, as it has a handy zipper compartment that I use to stash my credit card. While this is not the right present for a luxury bag fiend, it is a solid option for anyone in need of a purse for storing their essentials. Lauren Gould

Last year, my mom gave me the black and white colorway of these pyjamas – a smarter choice than, say, a holiday-themed set that I would neglect come New Year’s Day. Nearly 12 months and many washes later, these still feel silky soft. Wearing this matching set makes me feel put together at 10pm on a weekday, which I cannot say for the oversized designated sleep T-shirts I also rotate between. If you’re shopping for a picky person, a matching pyjama set is a universally appealing gift they will actually use. LG

This bracelet goes with everything, from workwear attire to loungewear. Like the earrings I tested from Mejuri (scroll below), it is so lightweight that I forget it is on my wrist. I also appreciate that it is adjustable, which reduces the chance the recipient will have to return it. It’s more personal than any old bracelet. You can grab the one that matches their birthstone (I’m an Aries diva, and tested the white diamond one). LG

Everyone seems to own J Crew’s trendy rollneck sweater. However, I rarely see anyone rocking the reversible iteration, which feels more unique and doubles as a cardigan. I have worn this with a simple black skirt, baggy jeans and even culottes. I bought this for my mom for her birthday this year, and she says it is the ideal piece for anyone who has hot flashes, thanks to its button-down design, which makes it less constricting than a regular sweater. LG

Last winter, I wrote about all the ways I style this small triangle scarf, including in my hair and around my waist. Nearly a year later, I am still wearing it to inject a little fun into the sea of neutrals I often wear. And while I have noticed a small thread has come loose, it otherwise remains in great condition. It is made of 100% merino wool, which makes it ideal for dressing up a basic coat in the winter or adding a pop of color to a simple sweater. Give this to someone who always looks put together and refuses to wear boring outfits, even when the weather is below zero. LG

“The quarter-zip has come roaring back into view as preppy has overtaken streetwear and athleisure as the fashion vernacular,” wrote Jess Carnter-Morley, the Guardian’s associate fashion editor. So, I knew my (mostly) stylish 23-year-old brother was the perfect candidate to test Sézane’s 100% wool quarter-zip sweater, which he said felt “warm and extremely comfortable”. This is a wonderful present for someone whose winter uniform is a sweater and jeans. LG

Made of 100% Italian wool, Sézane’s Stratford Square Scarf adds a touch of interest and extra warmth to an outfit. My brother, who tested the heather brown shade, found the scarf soft. I personally think the purple option, one of the trendiest colors of the season, would make a great gift for the man in your life not afraid to experiment with his look. Grab this for a stylish relative or significant other who usually compromises warmth for style (now, they will not have to). LG

To keep warm, Boston-based style coach Kin Moy suggests these men’s leather gloves for adding “a bit more gravitas than if you were stuffing your hands in your pocket”. This pair from Hestra is an ideal gift for a rugged guy who still loves a bit of luxury. “It manages to be really robust and sturdy,” which Moy said is great if your recipient is usually on snow shoveling duty. “They actually add a lot to an outfit,” Moy said.

These sweatpants are Moy’s tried-and-true Christmas present for men whose partners are fed up with their sloppy sweatpants. He says they are just as comfortable as a basic pair, but look more put together. “Everyone, client and friend or family who I’ve managed to convince to buy, they are like: ‘This has changed my life.’” LG

Moy personally owns Buck Mason’s 100% cotton beanie. “It fits really well,” he said, noting that it sits closer to your head unlike other, bulkier beanies. Gift this to the person whose winter hat could use a sleeker upgrade. LG

This trenchcoat is confidence in a jacket. Whenever I wear it, I feel like the most sophisticated, put-together version of myself. It has an oversized fit, but the collar and buttons lend it a bit of elegance. The cotton feels warm and thick and is the right weight for the tricky transitional months between seasons. I opted for classic camel, so as to let the rest of my outfits shine, but if you want a wintery version, it also comes in wool. As this runs large, I would recommend sizing down (especially if you are in between sizes). This would make a memorable gift for someone starting a new corporate job or building a capsule wardrobe. LG

Any Anthropologie employee knows about the Alani sweater – and anyone who receives this as a gift will be happy to – whether it be your stylish mom, in-law or friend who hates spending money on themselves. As a former sales associate, I can attest: this bestselling cashmere style was beloved by customers and staff alike. Even after testing far pricier sweaters, I still have not found something softer than this one. While I have a crewneck version that’s not currently sold, the mockneck design is an equally great gift. It’s also not too heavy, which makes it a wonderful transition piece come spring. LG

From the minute I brought this claw clip home, my roommate fell in love. She uses it to style her luscious, curly hair in a cute half-up, half-down look. And yes, $36 is a hefty price for a single claw clip – but it is the sort of frivolous item that makes a wonderful gift for a trendy tween or fashionable in-law. LG

I’m always disappointed when all my Bombas socks are in the laundry, forcing me to wear my inferior pairs. The ruffles help these strike a lovely balance between practical and fun, making them more exciting than a plain pair of tube socks. Gift these and a chocolate bar to a friend who constantly misplaces their socks. LG

I swear by scarves for elevating an otherwise bland outfit. This one, from J Crew, is a good entry-level option for the scarf-curious. It is made of 100% silk and comes in an array of colors, such as the classic smoked walnut one that I have styled with wide-leg jeans and a basic black top, around my purse and around my neck. If you need a present for a fashion lover who already has a closet full of denim, this is a fun accessory your giftee can use to spruce up their stuffed wardrobe. LG

If you are searching for jewelry for someone who refuses to let anything less than solid gold touch their earlobes, they will probably like this 10K yellow gold pair from Mejuri. These hoops are so tiny, I forget I am wearing them and unlike brass-plated ones I have tried, they don’t irritate my ears. Gift them to anyone building their solid gold jewelry collection or a minimalist who abhors flashy earrings. LG

Curated by Karen Yuan, who has covered food, kitchen gear and lifestyle for a decade. Her dream Christmas gift is a lifetime supply of cheesy ramen, and she has never turned down an invitation to hotpot.

These wobbly, jiggly fruit gels are made with gelatin and fruit purees such as guava, passion fruit, pineapple and coconut. They are sweetened with allulose and stevia instead of sugar, with some apple cider vinegar in the mix for gut health. They taste like a grown-up fruity vitamin gummy turned dessert and their whimsical gift box is decorated with the included molds (“square”, “orb” and “bundt”). KY

If they say they have everything, well, do they have a whole leg of Fermín Jamón Serrano? This variety comes from older, fattier pigs raised in Spain, and it is dry-cured for at least 18 months using artisanal methods in La Alberca, a Unesco World Heritage site. The result is a showstopper with deeply savory meat. If a gigantic leg of ham feels like too much of a gift (boo!), grab the Fermín Serranía sampler instead, which is sliced and ready to eat. KY

This California rosé forgoes alcohol in favor of a hemp-derived THC infusion; each pink bottle contains 15mg (about 3mg per glass), which gives you a nice, mellow buzz. Fair warning: its slightly tart, sour-beer-ish taste is a departure from traditional rosé, but it grew on me after a few sips. One for the friend who is drinking less but doesn’t feel like giving up wine entirely. KY

You probably know someone who has been really into sourdough since 2020. Get them Mark Bittman’s new whole-grain sourdough box, in which each loaf is made with just flour, water and salt, then frozen so you can finish baking it at home in about 20 minutes. There is even a small tub of salted butter included. The Half Wheat was my favorite, with a crackly crust and soft, chewy middle that fluffed right back up in the oven. The croissants stayed a little limp despite reheating – but their beautifully buttery flavor made up for it. KY

I spend an embarrassing amount of money on matcha lattes every month, so I have been trying to make them at home. The first-harvest, single-cultivar matcha in Muracha’s set comes from a family-run tea farm in Yame, Japan, and it is gloriously green with a bold, earthy taste. You also get a bamboo measuring spoon and a whisk, plus instructions that walk you through measuring, sifting and whisking in an “M” shape, which is fun to do. I pour it over soy milk for a latte that would cost at least $8 before tax and tip in a cafe. Rescue someone else whose matcha habit is getting out of hand. KY

Juno DeMelo, a Filter contributor, does not leave home without one of these tiny tins of Oregon sea salt. “I keep one in our camping bin and another in my purse so I can dial in the salt level of whatever I’m eating no matter where in the world I am,” she wrote. The sliding lid makes it easy to sprinkle salt wherever you happen to be eating. This trio includes flake salt, kosher salt and pinot noir-infused salt, each in a tin illustrated by an Oregon artist for a thoughtful stocking stuffer. KY

Fishwife took top honors for its tuna in our tinned fish taste test, but this brightly illustrated gift box contains 10 bestselling tins. Gould, the Filter editorial coordinator, also enjoyed its rainbow trout in chimichurri, giving it a 10/10 for flavor and texture. “This trout blows me away with its addition of grilled red pepper and herbs,” she wrote, praising how much flavor was packed into the little tin. KY

Did you forget a gift? Make it right with one of these dazzling charcuterie boards that ship overnight and arrive fully arranged and chilled. You can choose from the Classic holiday board (cheeses, meats, dried cherries, salted caramel walnuts, rosemary crackers and more on a reusable acacia board), the Thanksgiving board (nearly identical, except the big cheddar is shaped like a leaf instead of a candy cane), or the Jewish holiday board (not certified kosher, but cheeses are rennet-free). Nice for a host who does not need another bottle of wine as a gift, or someone far away you wish you could share a cheese plate with. KY

Some nights I want a bowl of pasta but have absolutely no interest in making a sauce. Pasta Dust offers a shortcut inspired by aglio e olio: cook pasta, save some of the starchy water and toss everything together with olive oil and a generous shake of the stuff, which combines garlic, herbs, spices and a little chili heat. It is like a fancier version of the packet of dried herbs that comes with instant ramen. Give this to the friend whose idea of cooking is boiling boxed pasta. KY

Tilden’s award-winning non-alcoholic cocktails are as complex as their boozy counterparts. The Lacewing combines cucumber, basil, lychee and juniper with a tingle of Sichuan pepper, while the Tandem leans moodier, with tart cherry, bitter orange, smoky lapsang tea and ginger. This six-pack includes three bottles of each. It is perfect for anyone who loves ordering a fancy bev, whether or not it is alcoholic. KY

These five little fish look convincingly like something you would find in the canned seafood aisle. Instead, they are made of 39% cacao milk chocolate. Buy it for the presentation more than the chocolate, which is smooth and creamy enough, but not best in class. It is a sweet gift for a tinned fish enthusiast or you could bring it to a white elephant exchange as a coveted prize. KY

I don’t really trust myself around a jar of this stuff. Made with California pistachios and organic oat milk powder, Pistakio’s rich spread tastes great on toast or swirled into Greek yogurt, though I also like to eat spoonfuls out of the jar. Give it to someone whose favorite gelato flavor is pistachio, or a home baker who could use a delicious shortcut. KY

Joy Supply, a small business launched this year, makes thin, buttery oat cookies with regeneratively farmed ingredients and a family recipe dating back to 1908. The White Chocolate Raspberry was a knockout flavor for me, equal parts sweet and tart, though all the cookies are extremely crumbly (eat them with great caution in a car, on the couch, etc). Gift a few boxes to someone who appreciates a good holiday cookie and a good backstory. KY
Curated by Juno DeMelo, who has covered health and fitness since 2007. If someone gave her a horse for Christmas, she would never ask for another gift for as long as she lives.

When my husband bought this gadget, I figured it would end up collecting dust in the back of a closet. But the pressure – delivered via 16 heated orbs that rotate in two directions at three speeds – is deep-tissue level, earning it a permanent place near the couch. I drape it over my neck and shoulders and press it into my lower back. Have a partner who is always begging you for a quick shoulder massage? This will make both of your lives better. Juno DeMelo

Made of BPA-free plastic and insulated with foam, the statement-making 64oz Silo is for anyone with lofty hydration goals. It weighs just more than 2lbs – or about half as much as Yeti’s metal jug of the same size – and keeps drinks cold for hours. Plus, it is dishwasher-safe, leakproof and virtually indestructible. JD

The muscles that support your head and neck are tough to reach without the help of a massage therapist ... or this tool. All you have to do is lie back and let the specially shaped nodules melt away stiffness at the base of your skull. Know someone who is tight from upper-body workouts, stress or just looking down at their phone too often? Of course you do – and this is the gift for them. JD

This set is great for giftees dedicated to their at-home workout regimen. It includes five latex bands spanning 3lb to 80lb of resistance, two clip-on handles, two ankle straps and a doorway anchor – and it is dead-simple to use. I keep the red band anchored in the doorway of my home office, where I use it for physical therapy exercises and accessory strength movements. JD

I am a longtime fan of Skida’s original brim hat for everyday wear. But for the runner or hiker in your life, the outdoor brand’s ventilated version can’t be beat. The featherweight hat has a crushable brim that packs down easily, UPF 50+ protection built into the brim and sides, and a moisture-wicking sweatband. JD

For the loved one who would never treat themself to a massage, but desperately needs one, there’s the Thera Cane. Six strategically placed treatment balls let you dig deep into otherwise hard-to-reach neck, back and shoulder muscles. Just find a knot and get to work, or try one of the easy-to-follow exercises in the accompanying instruction manual. JD

The Everywhere bag accompanies me, well, everywhere. You can style it as a fanny pack or crossbody bag, and it is the perfect size for holding a phone, keys, snack or a wallet. It is also the perfect prezzie for almost anyone: I have seen the bag (which comes in a dozen colors) on the shoulders and waists of teens, moms, dads and even celebs. JD

The ultra-lightweight, minimalist Xinglet relies on high-brilliance panels rather than battery-powered LEDs to keep you visible in low-light conditions. The stretchy waist and shoulder straps are fully adjustable, which makes it a thoughtful present for runners, cyclists and walkers of all ages and sizes. JD

I bought my first pair of Mexico 66s in 2009 and have been replacing them with a new pair roughly every eight years since. Originally developed for runners competing in the 1968 Summer Olympics, the go-with-anything sneakers have a soft leather upper and thin, flexible soles that make them comfortable right out of the box. And yet they are surprisingly sturdy, which is why I pack them on nearly every trip. Treat yourself or a frequent traveler to a pair. JD

Made from super-soft microfleece and available in men’s and women’s sizing, Stio’s Turpin joggers provide the exact right amount of warmth for light hiking in cool weather, aprés-ski and camping. Flatlock seams and a wide, low-profile waistband make for easy layering under ski pants or over wool tights – but honestly, even a couch potato would appreciate these cozy bottoms. JD

After running in these socks for nearly a decade, I can confidently say they hold up exceptionally well. I own four pairs, and here’s why: they have a right- and left-specific fit for a locked-in feel, a double-thick heel tab that prevents blisters, and a seamless toe box and heel cup that keep friction to a minimum. Stuff them in the stocking of a loved one who loves to run. JD

In my seemingly eternal quest to find the perfect workout leggings, I have often been disappointed. These holy grails offer just the right amount of compression, stay up and cost half as much as my “premium” leggings made from the exact same 77% nylon and 23% spandex blend. And because they come in eight colors and two lengths, I can’t think of a gym rat who wouldn ot be delighted to find these under the tree. JD

Curated by Heather Balogh Rochfort, who has covered hiking, camping and outdoor gear since 2005. Her favorite Christmas gift was technically her sister’s: a Creepy Crawlers oven. She can still conjure the smell of scorched plastic goop, which is either nostalgia or the fumes talking.

A water bottle with a built-in purifier sounds kind of gimmicky, but it turns out to be quite useful. It goes fly fishing with my family which means I don’t have to pack a separate filter and bottle: just scoop up some water from the river, press down on the internal chamber, and you’ve got a bottle of drinkable water ready to go. From anglers to rafters and backpackers, it’s a great gift for anyone who spends a lot of time on (or near) fresh water. Heather Balogh Rochfort

Kari Traa is perhaps the best-known name in women’s base layers and for good reason. The fun patterns and colors give women a chance to show off their style. The Smekker is one of my favorite layers to wear during my 50-plus ski days each season in Aspen because I can take it from the chairlift to the après and still look good. HBR

The MegaMat is the most popular car-camping pad on the market, most likely because it turns sleeping on the dirt into a cloud-like experience. At 4in thick, it is so comfortable that my 70-year-old mother doesn’t mind using it. And it is reasonably priced compared with its plush competitors, making it a great gift for outdoorsy folks who want to camp without back pain. HBR

The Redwood reminds me of sleep away camp with the Girl Scouts (ah, memories!), but – unlike the sleeping bags of my youth – also insanely warm. It is my go-to when I sleep in the back of my Subaru Outback at trailheads, and it is so toasty. Fair warning: it is the heaviest sleeping bag I have ever picked up. That makes it the perfect gift for a car camper or van lifer, since it will never leave the trunk. HBR

When plans change by the hour, the R1 Air Fleece keeps up. This shirt is warm, cozy and versatile. I wear it for shoulder-season hikes and ski days, and I will throw it on with jeans in my small mountain town. My husband wears his on cold-weather fly-fishing trips, and I recently spotted a friend wearing hers at a Red Rocks concert. If you have a sweatshirt lover on your list, this is the one to replace it. HBR

Mountain Hardwear’s hooded jacket is like yoga pants for your arms. You get the warmth of a down jacket, but it is super stretchy thanks to flexible fabric and welded (instead of stitched) seams. I have broader shoulders and it makes the jacket far more comfortable when I am hiking. HBR

This long-handled titanium spoon is the best tool for digging into dehydrated meal bags without getting food all over your sleeves. It weighs less than an ounce, making it an easy stocking stuffer for anyone who spends nights on the trail. (Every backpacker I know has one or wants another.) HBR

I will die on this hill: every person who squats when they pee needs a pee rag. The Kula Cloth has an absorbent, antimicrobial side for wiping and a waterproof side that keeps your hands dry and it snaps right on to your pack. No more drip-drying or packing out soggy toilet paper. HBR

These bendable, rubber-coated twist ties can do no wrong. I take a few on every single trip, whether I’m backcountry skiing, backpacking or mountain biking. I have used them to fix pulk sleds, shoes, busted tents, backpack straps and more. Stocking stuffer price, MVP-level usefulness and there is not a single outdoorsy person who doesn’t need a few. HBR

Curated by Adam Doud, who has been covering tech of all shapes and sizes for 15 years. His favorite Christmas gift is always Lego: any Lego, all Lego, nothing but the Lego. A close second is the Stargate SG-1 boxed set.

This little speaker is surprisingly powerful considering its size and the rainbow lights add a fun touch anywhere – my daughter stole mine to hang from the handlebars of her bike. It is also great for backpackers who want to bring along big sound without the weight. Adam Doud

The Amazfit Active 2 gives you all the best functionality of a more expensive smartwatch – step tracking, exercise detection and even a very good AI assistant – in a design nobody would guess is a smartwatch. Get it for someone who is just starting to take exercise more seriously or someone who is always misplacing their phone. You can ring it from your wrist. AD

Our pick for best seat cushion is a great gift for anyone who regularly logs eight hours or more sitting down – whether that is working at their laptop or playing a game. It eases back pain and turns any chair into the best seat in the house: I use mine every day at my kitchen table and I love it. AD

Magnetic battery packs are getting thinner and lighter these days, and this one is so petite you will forget it is there. Press it into the hand of your teenager whose phone is dying all the time or a construction worker who spends all day away from an outlet and give them the gift of an extra half a day of juice. AD

The little light on a cellphone can’t compare to a proper flashlight like Olight’s ArkPro, my personal favorite. It has a powerful spotlight, flood light, UV light and even a laser pointer, which makes it a fantastic gift for pet owners whose fur babies love chasing the magic dot. AD

Know an older relative who has not taken the plunge on streaming yet? Roku makes the easiest way to get them up to speed. The simple interface will feel familiar to the cable remote they are used to and the feature-packed 4K version will not need replacing for years. Just budget in some time to help grandma set it up – that is part of the gift. AD

For nearly $80, these earbuds are a really good value, with a fun, transparent design, excellent sound and very decent active noise-cancellation. If your teenager’s AirPods are always dying or your spouse spends hours on the train every day, give them the gift of reliability – you also get a solid eight-hour work day on a single charge with a couple more charges in the case. AD

Even Amazon’s most basic Kindle is a phenomenal e-reader that the bookworm in your life will welcome with open arms. And they are not stuck buying books from Amazon. Pairing it with the Libby app makes it easy to borrow ebooks from your local library in seconds, totally free. AD

This car power outlet plug has two retractable power cables that extend up to 3.1ft, then neatly coil up inside to tidy the tangle. It as a fantastic all-in-one solution that makes a great gift for anyone who spends a lot of time driving – or chauffeuring a kid who can never seem to stay charged. AD

This mouse folds into a tiny cube, then it unfolds into an arch for a cute little ergonomic mouse with two buttons and a touch sensitive slider/scroll wheel. It is great for someone who works remotely and is always on the go – never working in the same place twice. AD

If you know someone nostalgic for the BlackBerry days, or just hopelessly clumsy with a virtual keyboard, this is an easy buy. This magnetic keyboard attaches to the back of your phone and slides down for when you need to pound out a quick email or text message. True to its name, it also has a power bank that can top off your phone at the same time. AD

My go-to travel bag, the TomToc T24 sling holds a surprising amount of stuff inside its main pouch, and has multiple pockets inside for a laptop, a tablet, a water bottle and several other small pouches. Give it to a friend who never leaves home without too many gadgets in tow. AD

Give your own household the gift of organization. The Skylight Calendar 2 is a 15in display that hangs on your wall and syncs with Google, Outlook and most other calendars. Besides displaying upcoming events, there are some neat features including meal planning (which can populate your shopping lists) and the ability to add events to your calendar by taking a photo of an event poster. AD
Curated by Lauren Gould, who interviewed multiple tweenagers to find out what they really want.
Charlie, a 12-year-old, wants clothing from Free People Movement. “I think it’s a really good brand. It’s fashionable and sporty,” she said. LG
“That seems to be popular. I think everyone, mostly friends at school, wants to listen to music, and they are just the popular brand,” said Ollie, a 17-year-old. LG
“I’m asking for a lot of sweatshirts from this one brand called Madhappy. I love sweats and anything comfortable,” said 14-year-old Riley. LG
“This is a me thing, though. I used to watch the show a lot and I like seeing them hit each other,” said 10-year old Axel. LG

I first visited the Miffy store on a recent trip to Kyoto, Japan, and fell in love with this cartoon bunny. My sample of its Advent calendar, postcards, stickers and playing cards are all decorated with delightful illustrations of Miffy and her friends, and would make a great gift for a tween or teen who loves cute cartoon characters. LG

Curated by Tracy Allison and Nick Mokey. As Tux the tuxedo cat’s human, Allison has covered countless cat products. Her favorite Christmas gift she got was a multipack of Scotch tape at age five, which she used to try to fix a broken vintage doorknob.

Mokey is forever battling a plume of pet fur from his dog Marty and two cats, Daphne and Niles. His favorite Christmas gift was a Radio Shack RC truck he got when he was 10. Waiting for a battery to charge has never been more agonizing.

I have had enough pets over the years to know that an animal’s aches and pains are not always obvious. Now that my cat Tux is officially in the double digits, I am becoming more proactive about making his long-term comfort a priority, particularly considering how active he has been throughout his life. Made with contoured memory foam for orthopedic support and with a heated cover for gentle warmth, this therapeutic bed is my top pick for cats with aging joints. It may be on the pricier side, but for a cat who spent his youth sleeping under cars, I figure he has earned a little luxury. Tracy Allison

My cat is a window napper, which means his favorite sleeping spots can get extra chilly in the winter, so I bought him this heating pad before a big snow storm. After some trial and error with the settings, I discovered he is happiest with it on the lowest heat and an extra towel layered on top. TA

This is my go-to affordable gift for cat lovers. It mounts to the corner of a wall or door frame, avoiding the tripping hazard some other cat products create. Tux uses his whenever he’s vying for a little extra attention or looking to self-soothe. If a cat doesn’t take to it right away, a spritz of catnip spray can help pique their interest. TA

I switched to this elevated dish after Tux kept managing to push his lightweight bowl under a nearby bar cart. This sturdier bowl stays put more easily and means less crouching for a more comfortable mealtime. TA

I have dreamed of being an automatic litter box person, but my cat refused any enclosed box I tried to introduce. This stainless steel litter box has been the best compromise I have found: it helps keep odors in check, and the high sides give him something to wipe his paws against instead of using the wall. TA

Tux had already taken to kneading on a black fuzzy throw when I came across the concept of a “mama blanket” on Reddit. Essentially, it is any soft, fluffy blanket your cat likes to knead on for comfort. It’s a rare cat gift we can both enjoy equally: he is not a particularly cuddly cat, but on cold winter nights, he will curl up close if I am using “mama blanket” too. TA

My 105lb Pyrenees mutt Marty shreds garden-variety dog toys into heaps of stuffing within minutes, but Tuffy toys somehow survive for years, even when left in the Pacific north-west rain. The Ultimate Ring is easy to toss like a frisbee and the chain link offers a nice handle for tug of war. But if I am feeling generous this year, Marty may find Destructosaurus under the tree. Nick Mokey

Look, I don’t eat lamb, but somebody does, so our dogs might as well enjoy their (apparently delicious) leftover lungs. These dehydrated delights have a light, foam-like texture that snaps cleanly to whatever size you want and crucially, leaves no smell or residue on your hands. Every dog I have met adores them. NM

A solid dog treat pouch is a dispenser of good-boy affirmations for dogs and a reprieve from crumby pockets for humans. Marty has easily destroyed half a dozen treat bags in his lifetime, giving me an opportunity to test plenty. This is the one I keep coming back to. It clips to a belt or pocket effortlessly, the drawstring keeps treats from bouncing out, and the poop-bag pocket has room for two rolls, so you are never caught empty-handed. NM
Curated by Yuan and Gould based on our readers’ most beloved items of the past year.

When we blind taste-tested 10 premium chocolate bars, Hu’s vegan bars were a hit. We especially love the rich cashew butter folded into dark chocolate with raspberry filling, but Hu also offers bars with hazelnut butter, almond butter with puffed quinoa and more. KY

A cleaning brush may be an odd choice, but at just over $4 per scrubber, this is one of our most popular budget recs of all time, plus it has plastic-free, natural coconut fibers. Give your friends and family the gift of peace of mind that comes with avoiding microplastics. KY

Our priciest but prettiest stocking stuffer (and it lasts much longer than chocolates and drinks): this oyster has a hand-stitched felted wool shell and a little white pearl tucked inside. The wool is fairly traded and made in Kyrgyzstan and the whole thing is ready to hang with a string attached. KY

In testing, this sleep mask beat out 31 competitors to become our overall favorite, then went on to become one of our most popular recommendations of all time (our readers are a sleepy bunch). It gives total blackout coverage and stays comfortable enough to wear all night or a whole plane flight. KY

Last winter, I tried No Particular Order’s acquaintance cards, a dating app alternative that forces you to get off Hinge and approach someone in real life. They make a fun stocking stuffer for a friend tired of swiping or a newly single family member eager to reenter the dating scene. The cards recently got an updated design with a more durable tin and an included pencil. LG

Sipped from a festive can, this alcohol-free Negroni has all the bittersweet notes of the real thing, plus a little bit of juniper and citrus. I find it less sweet than the other NA-gronis in the beverage aisle. KY
Other pieces you might enjoy from the Filter, the Guardian’s guide to buying fewer, better things:
The nine best personalized gifts, from a timeless tote bag to custom stationery
The 17 best gift ideas for the person who already has everything
German knives, English socks: 13 gifts beloved globally that Americans are missing out on

items.title: This tiny gamepad with dual analog thumbsticks pushes the limits of portable controllers
paragraphs: As much as I appreciate the ingenious design of the Nintendo Switch’s Joy-Con, my family and I can’t stand using them as standalone gamepads. So when we travel with the Switch 2, we always bring at least one full-size gamepad, plus a couple of 8BitDo’s Zero 2 controllers for games that don’t use analog thumbsticks. I’ve spent years hunting for an alternative that pairs the size of the Zero 2 with as much of the functionality of a larger controller as I can get, and CRKD’s new Atom Plus is nearly exactly that. But if you have larger hands like I do, you may find the gamepad’s focus on portability a struggle.

Measuring around 3.5 inches wide, the $29.99 Atom Plus is about a half-inch smaller than the 8BitDo Zero 2 but squeezes in considerably more features and functionality. The most obvious is a pair of symmetrical analog thumbsticks with anti-drift tunneling magnetoresistance technology. You also get shoulder buttons and triggers, rumble feedback, a dedicated home button, motion controls, and customization through a mobile app.

Like many third-party controllers, the Atom Plus works with multiple platforms, including the Switch and Switch 2, PCs, Android, iOS, and various smart TVs. And just like other gamepads, pairing to different devices requires putting the Atom Plus into one of several Bluetooth modes by holding down a combination of buttons at power-up, which in this case is the home button plus a specific direction on the D-pad. It’s easy to do, but never easy to remember: I frequently needed to grab the manual or quickly Google which direction I need to press when switching devices. The Atom Plus already features a bunch of technical info etched into the back of the controller, so I’d love to see these important pairing instructions included there, too. (And that goes for all multiplatform gamepads.)

I primarily tested the Atom Plus with the Nintendo Switch 2 since I mostly plan to use the controller as a travel accessory. The thumbsticks are about the same size as those on the original Switch Joy-Con, which means they’re smaller than the Switch 2’s. And while I prefer an asymmetrical layout, the Atom Plus’ sticks are very good, with a little more tension than Nintendo’s that I find actually helps with precision movements given their limited travel.

While the overall build quality feels excellent, the Atom Plus’ tiny footprint creates some compromises and challenges. The front action buttons and D-pad feel nice and squishy, but the gamepad’s controls are a little crowded. When pressing down or right on the D-pad, my thumb regularly bumps the left thumbstick. It doesn’t hinder gameplay, but I do find it an annoying distraction.

The shoulder buttons use digital microswitches, as do the triggers, which means the latter can’t be used for racing games that support analog acceleration controls. I like that the two sets of buttons on the top edge sit at slightly different heights, but I would have preferred a little more differentiation since I’ve occasionally accidentally pressed the triggers when I meant to hit the shoulder buttons.

I was impressed with the Atom Plus’ customizability, however. When paired to an accompanying mobile app, you can check the controller’s remaining charge, turn off rumble feedback, see its unique product number (by tapping your phone to an NFC chip inside the controller), and remap any of its controls. That includes the pair of dual-function shortcut levers that replicate the Switch’s plus and minus buttons and screenshot shortcut.

Those levers move up and down and cleverly reduce the number of buttons crowding the front of the Atom Plus, but they feel a little too small, which is more or less the general theme. It’s a tiny gamepad that’s great for travel or stashing in your everyday carry. But, unsurprisingly, it probably won’t find its way into your regular gaming rotation. It’s assumed that players will be willing to settle for the compromise of occasionally contorting their fingers in weird, new ways for one of the smallest fully featured controllers on the market.

I don’t think a dual-stick controller could get any smaller than the Atom Plus without making too many ergonomic compromises. So while I applaud CRKD for the careful balancing act behind the Atom Plus’ design, and would certainly recommend it for those wanting a very capable controller that’s also cheap and portable, I’m now curious how it compares to Microsoft’s recently announced Xbox Nano controller that’s “surprisingly comfortable,” according to The Verge’s Tom Warren. It’s $20 more expensive than CRKD’s and noticeably larger, but it adds analog triggers, a more spacious design, and stubby grips making it easier to hold for those of us with beefy mitts.

items.title: How AdHoc made Dispatch feel like an animated TV series
paragraphs: Dispatch looks, sounds, and plays like an animated TV show, and that was deliberate: AdHoc wanted it to be a no-barrier entry point for people who don't usually play games. A year after its launch on 22 October 2025, the episodic superhero workplace comedy has more than five million players, and the new Dispatch Deluxe Edition offers new ways to play, including replacing its graphics with storyboard art.

The game stars Breaking Bad's Aaron Paul as Robert Robertson, a former hero turned dispatcher for a team of reformed supervillains, alongside Jeffrey Wright, Laura Bailey, and members of the Critical Role cast. Getting that cast to feel like they're in the same room, and getting the player to feel part of the story, took a lot of invisible work.

You can read how four video tracks and a doughnut shop gave Dispatch its start, but here I ask co-founders Nick Herman and Dennis Lenart, the studio's COO and CTO, and both co-creative directors, how they nailed down the premium animation.

How do you keep dialogue, facial expressions and performances consistent when the player can send a scene in different directions? While it was made using Unreal Engine 5, it starts on the page. "Everything is written with choice in mind," says Herman.

AdHoc built its own tools to ingest scripts, including a playable script you can read and click through. That produces the recording script actors use in the booth, which Herman says is "a little bit crazy to read on a linear page". Do it long enough, though, and it starts to make sense. Each scene has a spine, and every time a choice appears, different options eventually trunk back into the main flow.

The studio also uses recordings as a directing tool. AdHoc ingests every performance as it’s captured, so when an actor records opposite someone already in the booth, the team can play those existing lines back for them to react to. In Herman’s example, with Aaron Paul already recorded, the team can bring in Erin as Blonde Blazer, play Paul’s lines for her to read off, then play him again after her response. It’s a clever bit of craft: AdHoc builds each conversation around real delivery. The effect, Herman says, is to simulate the actors being in the same room, which helps performances feel grounded and integrated. It also gives a scene its flow, because the actors know where they’re coming in from, and it makes testing branches easy.

It's clever craft. Rather than recording actors in isolation and hoping the performances fit together later, AdHoc builds the conversation around real delivery. The effect, Herman says, is to simulate the actors being in the same room, which helps performances feel grounded and integrated. It also gives a scene its flow, because the actors know where they're coming in from, and it makes testing branches easy.

By the time animation begins, the voice work is trusted, and the team is happy with it. The facial animation then comes down to knowing every character. "Not everyone laughs the same. When they cry, they look different," Herman says. "Every character is their own person. Like they are on the page, they are in animation." Getting there takes "a lot of review, a lot of ref", and the team shoots plenty of reference footage for its animators.

For AdHoc, the problem was the seam: the point where a cutscene ends and gameplay begins. “The goal was always to make it feel integrated,” Lenart says. Part of the studio’s philosophy is that gameplay and story should feel like a seamless handoff rather than two different experiences. He and Herman had worked on plenty of games with clear story sections and clear gameplay sections, “and you could feel that break every single time”. That, he says, “always kind of drove us crazy”.

When they dreamed of starting their own studio, one mandate was to choose mechanics that feel like an integrated part of a character's life, not scenes contrived for interactivity. If someone has to break into a room and pick a lock, it shouldn't be something the character would never do.

For Dispatch, that meant the shift mechanic. Robert sends heroes out on calls because it's his job. "It's the thing he does every day," says Lenart. "So, when he sits down at his computer to do it, it feels natural."

The team also made sure the Z-Team keep talking to the player throughout each shift, so the dialogue and relationships keep flowing, and the story never stops for gameplay. At times, a shift cuts out to a cinematic and back in again, and Lenart says that only feels organic because "we spent a lot of time and effort to make it that way".

Herman and Lenart both spent years at Telltale Games, the studio behind The Walking Dead, The Wolf Among Us, and Tales from the Borderlands, and Dispatch forced them to drop much of their old way of working.

At Telltale, Lenart says, cinematics were "fast and loose". Episodes were made in what the studio called live development: they would release one episode, then spend the next six weeks on the following. Things "could change at any time". Player feedback from the previous episode could feed straight back in, with tweaks to cinematics and character intentions right up until the day before shipping.

Dispatch had a different goal. AdHoc wanted the visuals and style to feel like "a premium animated television show" that wasn't a barrier for people who might enjoy a story like this but aren't typically into games. That meant a more traditional animation pipeline, with decisions made much earlier and, in some cases, locked down a year in advance.

"That was a really big learning curve for us since we were used to being able to make small adjustments all the way up until the last minute," Lenart says. But he now thinks the discipline made the game better. It "forced many detailed conversations way earlier in the process, which only better informed how each piece of the story was going to play out". His verdict: "Oh, this is actually the way to make the best quality product."
The Dispatch Deluxe Edition is out now on PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X, and Nintendo Switch / Switch 2, and $10.99 digital upgrade path for existing owners
