items.title: Eurovision is finally coming to Asia - meet the stars gearing up to take the stage
paragraphs: On Saturday, the biggest and longest-running international song contest will make a leap into unknown territory.

Eurovision, the pan-European competition famed for zany gimmicks, slick, sometimes over-the-top staging, the drama of its complex voting system and, occasionally, for outstanding music, celebrates its 70th birthday this year.
And to mark it, the European Broadcasting Union is trying out audiences in Asia.
It's an idea that's been talked about for two decades but never materialised, despite many false starts.
Until now - Eurovision Asia will hold its first grand final in Bangkok, starting at 20:30 ICT (13:30 GMT).

Transferring one of the most successful television formulas that has worked in Europe for 70 years to Asia has not been straightforward, says Sarun 'Note' Kungbunpot, a Eurovision enthusiast and Thai singer who has won several competitions in this region.
"It's still very new in Asia. I'm not sure many people have heard about it yet," he says, adding that he thinks it will take a bit of time for audiences to adjust.
"When we look at contests in Thailand, the Philippines and Korea, we actually compete based on the singer.
"It's all about popularity – fans are looking for their idols. But Eurovision is all about the song, not the singer. I think this needs to be communicated clearly."

Then there is the long history of Eurovision in Europe. It began in 1956 as a project to encourage greater cultural exchanges in a Europe which was trying to forge a common future after two world wars.

This was the very start of the age of mass television ownership, and Eurovision became such a fixture it is now an indelible piece of Europe's shared cultural heritage. It has no such resonance in Asia, and arrives in this region in the digital age, when traditional TV formats are struggling to cut through.

Only 11 countries are taking part in this first Eurovision Asia contest – host Thailand, along with Malaysia, the Philippines, Vietnam, Cambodia, Laos, South Korea, Mongolia, Bangladesh, Nepal and Bhutan.
Asian giants India, China, Japan and Indonesia are noticeably absent, although there are negotiations ongoing to try to get them into next year's contest, assuming there is one.
There have also been problems with the organisation of this event.

A sudden million-dollar (£760,000) budget cut just three weeks before the final meant many of the technicians familiar with staging Eurovision were not brought to Thailand, and there have been a number of staff resignations too.
Eurovision fans - and there are many passionate followers around the world - have noticed, criticising audio and lighting in rehearsal videos.

In Europe, there have long been reports of co-ordinated voting to back neighbours, for example the four Nordic countries voting for each other. This seems less likely in Eurovision Asia, but political differences, for example between Thailand and Cambodia after their border war last year, could influence how their audiences vote.

Filipinos, with their passion for singing, are expected to be enthusiastic participants and the 11 million who live overseas might make a difference. But as most live and work in countries which are not participating, their votes will only go into the "rest of the world" pool.

For Bhutan, with a population of less than a million, this is a rare chance to shine on a global stage, which puts some pressure on 24-year-old Thukten Nyendra, the singer representing the Himalayan kingdom in Bangkok with his song Lhayi Semo (The Angel). Before coming here he had never left his country or been on a plane before.

"I'm not a star. I'm just Nyendra over there," he told the BBC. "Nobody knows me. But Eurovision has given me a huge platform. Actually winning would mean the world to us... If I really make it through all of this, it would mean the entire freaking world to us."

11 different size formats comprise this collection of office booths by British furniture brand Boss Design.
Mews pods feature ribbed privacy glass, as well as adjustable light, noise and ventilation levels to create a comfortable and productive working environment.

Estonian brand Silen‘s Space Gen 2 collection of office pods are made from a pioneering cassette system, meaning that its 50-per-cent-recycled-aluminium frame can withstand multiple disassemblies, relocations and reassemblies.
It also features a signature “floating roof”, which the brand says enhances air flow, as well as acoustic properties to maintain privacy and focus during calls and work sessions.
Collective RailLock ceiling system by The Collective
Aesthetic interest and sound dampening meet in this ceiling-mounted system by British company The Collective.
Collective RailLock comprises slabs and fins made from PET felt and aluminium fixings, which come in various shapes and colourways to fit diverse interior styles.
Spanish workplace furniture manufacturer Actiu has evolved its QYOS acoustic pods to allow for enhanced customisation options and control when in use.
A choice of exterior panels and planters and interior options, including soft or hard seating, various table heights and screen mounts meet climate and acoustic controls for enhanced user experience.
Office furniture brand Mute has further updated its Jetson office pod range to enhance the booths’ versatility and configurability.
New Jetson pods now feature more options for wall configurations – ranging from mainly glazed to solid, opaque walls – and come in a choice of 24 colourways.
Zonify Wall and Zonify Table by Studio Stockholm for Zilenzio

Acoustic solutions brand Zilenzio worked with Studio Stockholm on Zonify Wall – a large, wall-mounted acoustic panel – and matching Zonify Table, which has a side-lit smaller screen for use as a desk backboard.
Both products feature pleated fabric, forming a dimensional surface that plays with light and shadow as well as absorbing sound for a quieter and calmer interior.

items.title: What could El Niño mean for winter weather in the US and Canada?
paragraphs: Montreal, Canada was badly hit by the Great Ice Storm of 1998 which was blamed, in part, on El Niño.
The developing El Niño - already the strongest on record by some measures - continues to grow and could have profound effects on the weather across North America this autumn and winter.
The naturally-occurring climate phenomenon sees trade winds over the Pacific Ocean, which usually blow from east to west, weakening or reversing with warm water instead spreading eastwards.
This releases heat into the atmosphere which can drive major shifts in global weather patterns.
Impacts in the US and Canada are varied, with a greater chance of a warm and dry winter in northern areas and more risk of flooding rain further south.
There is also some evidence that El Niño can increase the likelihood of disruption to the stratospheric polar vortex which can, in turn, bring snowfall later in winter.
No two El Niños are the same and the impacts are not guaranteed - the odds are just shifted in favour of certain outcomes.
The eastward shift of warm ocean waters associated with El Niño can cause the Pacific jet stream to move south and extend eastwards, directing rain-bearing weather systems across the southern USA.
This typically leads to wetter winters during El Niño years.
The likely impacts of El Niño on winter weather vary across different parts of North America.
The latest three month forecast, external from the US National Weather Service (NWS) suggests this is a likely outcome for the winter of 2026-2027.
South-eastern states, including Florida, Georgia and the Carolinas, have the greatest chance of seeing above-average rainfall.
The El Niño winter of 1997-1998 brought significant flooding in the south-east and spun up tornadoes for Florida.
Severe flooding hit Long Beach, California in February 2024.
California could well find itself in the firing line with forecasts suggesting a wet winter is likely.
Governor Gavin Newsom has already declared a state of emergency, external ahead of anticipated floods and mudslides.
Areas scarred by recent wildfires are particularly susceptible, with the effects of climate change exacerbating the risks.

Many past El Niños have been wet here, with winter 2023-2024 bringing relief from drought. However this is not always the case. In the strong El Niño of 2015-2016, California actually had below-average rainfall.
Coastal erosion and large waves could be worsened by a rise in the overall sea level driven by so-called Kelvin waves.
This is where ocean water which sloshes eastwards across the Pacific due to El Niño reaches the west coast of the Americas, where it can travel no further.
It causes a large-scale wave which then spreads along the coast over a period of weeks and months, raising sea levels by 15cm (6in) or more.
The shift of the Pacific jet stream generally leads to warmer and milder winters in the north-west USA, Northern Plains and Ohio Valley - as well as western and central Canada.
This lessens the risk of flooding, but reduced rainfall can leave groundwater and river levels low, fuelling drought and wildfires in spring and summer.
Ski resorts can also suffer from a lack of snow.
Long-range predictions suggest a dry, warm winter is more likely than usual this year.
However, El Niño does not guarantee this. For instance, the winters of 1982-1983 and 2015-2016 were wetter than normal in the north-west USA.
In much of the northern USA, and large swathes of Canada, a greater chance of dry and warm weather makes snow less likely.
Further south, however, above-average precipitation typically leads to big snowfalls in the Californian mountains and southern Rockies - good news for water stocks.
It can also increase the probability of snow at lower levels in the southern and eastern USA - but only if enough cold air is in the mix.
The area around Washington DC often receives more snowfall than usual in an El Niño winter - but not always.
Snowfall caused chaos in Washington DC in February 2010.
The winter of 2009-2010 delivered record-breaking snowfall that brought the city to a standstill, while widespread blizzards affected much of the US east coast in 2016.
However, some of Washington DC's least snowy winters have also occurred during El Niño events, including 1972-1973 and 1997-1998 which brought just 0.1in (0.25cm) of snow.
Higher winter temperatures in eastern Canada and the north-east USA can mean precipitation that might normally fall as snow gives rain instead.
This can increase the chance of freezing rain events, with the so-called Great Ice Storm of 1998, external being blamed partly on the effects of El Niño.
It is worth saying that snowfall amounts are decreasing overall in most places due to human-induced climate change, meaning predicting the impact of El Niño is even more complex.
An added complication is the possible impact of El Niño on the polar vortex, a ring of strong winds that circles the North Pole in winter, around 10-30 miles (16-48km) up in the stratosphere.
It holds cold, dense air in place above the Arctic but sometimes it can weaken and disrupt, and there is some evidence that the energy released into the atmosphere by El Niño makes this more likely.
Disruptions to the polar vortex sometimes ripple down through the atmosphere, weakening the polar jet stream and opening the door for cold air to spill across Canada and the USA.
However this does not always occur and the links are far from clear.

items.title: Ocean liner sunk in Florida to become "world's largest artificial reef"
paragraphs: On Wednesday, the ocean liner SS United States was sunk 180 feet underwater to become an artificial reef off the coast of Florida.
The sinking took approximately eight hours, and dozens of onlookers and officials looked on as the ship underwent a controlled deployment, or scuttling, to the bottom of the ocean.
The ship will join a long stretch of artificial reefs, including 580 other decommissioned vessels and structures, that line the ocean floor off the coast Destin-Fort Walton Beach, Florida.

“A new chapter has begun in Destin-Fort Walton Beach, Florida, where the legendary SS United States, once the fastest ocean liner in the world, has completed her final voyage to become the World’s Largest Artificial Reef,” said a release from the government of Destin-Fort Walton Beach.
The site serves as a tourist and dive destination for SCUBA divers both new and seasoned, as the underwater structures are meant to provide infrastructure for marine life.
“Beyond its appeal as a dive destination, the SS United States will serve an important environmental purpose,” said the team.
“Her massive structure will provide new habitat for marine life, supporting the growth of an underwater ecosystem that includes inhabitants such as sea turtles, grouper, snapper and marlin.”
In preparation for its scuttling, the ship underwent a years-long remediation process, where it was stripped of toxic materials, such as green neotex exterior floor covering and paint.
Elements such as the ventilation system, wiring and the propeller were also removed, with the latter stored for a land-based museum that will accompany the dive site.
“To see a project of this magnitude become a reality is an incredible moment for our team and for the future of marine conservation,” said Destin-Fort Walton Beach natural resources chief Alex Fogg.

“This is so much more than creating a new dive destination. It’s an opportunity to advance marine science on a scale we’ve never experienced before. The sheer scale of the SS United States presents a rare opportunity to study how an artificial reef of this size transforms over time.”
The project has been years in the making. The ship, designed by naval architect William Francis Gibb and known for its speed, served as a passenger vessel between 1952 and 1969.

It was decommissioned in 1969, and eventually bought to a Philadelphia harbour in the 1990s, where it sat inactive for decades as various owners bought and then sold the vessel in failed attempts to restore it and make it profitable.
In 2009, the non-profit SS United States Conservancy purchased and began stewarding the ship.
In 2024, due to rent issues, the ship could no longer stay berthed at its Philadelphia pier, and the SS United States Conservancy sold it to Okaloosa County, Florida, for $1 million.
As of today, it stands upright in its intended position, and its uppermost deck is accessible to divers, who can “now enjoy the site”.

Other artificial reefs around the world include the Reefline project in Miami, which is set to feature underwater sculpture designed by OMA and a LEGO-inspired modular system designed by Alex Goad, intended to restore damaged coral reefs.
Photography courtesy of Destin-Fort Walton Beach

items.title: Catherine Zeta-Jones says US move humbled her before big break with Steven Spielberg
paragraphs: Catherine Zeta Jones moved to California in the 1990s to pursue an acting career
Catherine Zeta-Jones has said she had an ego check after moving to America in the 1990s.

The Swansea-born star had become a household name in the UK, but Hollywood quickly provided a reality check for the rising star and she was even asked by casting agents if she had any acting experience.
It was during her stint on CBS mini-series Titanic that she was seen by Steven Spielberg who suggested she go for a role in The Mask of Zorro, which he was producing.
"Five days later I got the job, and three days after that, I was down there starting my sword-fighting lessons," she said.
Zeta-Jones had become a star in the UK thanks to her breakout role in The Darling Buds of May that originally aired from 1991 to 1993.
But when she touched down in California, she was no longer recognised by the public and had a six-month visa to "give America a shot".
She told Business Insider, external it was "good" for her to have her ego knocked down a bit.
It was only when the Spielberg saw the Titanic series that she was given a major opportunity.
"I was shipped down to Mexico to screen test with Antonio Banderas," she said.
Catherine Zeta-Jones and Antonio Banderas at a premiere for The Mask of Zorro in 1998
She credits it as her breakthrough into A-list territory and it was rumoured that she beat actors such as Salma Hayek and Jennifer Lopez to the part.
Zeta-Jones went on to work with Sean Connery in Entrapment which cemented her stardom, and she refers to the late James Bond actor as a "dear force of nature".
"I just never wanted to stop acting with him, because we were such good buddies," she said.
"He was so incredibly protective of me, like a daughter he never had, and he said that to me."
Zeta-Jones says it has been "liberating" to use her Welsh accent in Kill Jackie
Zeta-Jones is currently starring in Kill Jackie, a revenge thriller based on the 2018 novel The Price You Pay by Nick Harkaway.
She stars as the titular Jackie Price, a Welsh high-end art dealer with a shady past in the drug trade who discovers a hit has been put out on her.
In September, Zeta-Jones made headlines for revealing that it was the first time she had used her Swansea accent for a role.
After decades of working on accents including English, American and Scottish she said the opportunity to speak in her native accent was both "liberating and cathartic".
As well as returning to her Welsh roots, the series' ultra-violent scenes have been a blast for Zeta-Jones, who relished the chance to go off the rails.
"I wanted the audience to come along on this ride with me and root for her. In all the craziness."

items.title: Police investigating David Walliams over reports alleging serious sexual offences
paragraphs: The Metropolitan Police has launched an investigation into David Walliams over reports of "alleged serious sexual offences".
It comes after ITV News and the Guardian published reports alleging that Walliams had been accused of sexual misconduct by several women.

The Met said that the allegations being investigated are separate from those reported by ITV and the Guardian, but as "part of their investigation, detectives are also proactively reviewing that reporting to establish whether there is any evidence of offences".
When those allegations were first reported, Walliams said he was "not a sexual predator" and had not "broken the law".
In a statement released on Friday, the Met said it had "received a number of allegations of non-recent serious sexual offences involving a man now in his 50s".
"Those who have come forward are being supported by specialist officers," the statement added.
Detective Superintendent Mike Cagney said: "We would encourage anyone who has been the victim of a sexual offence to come forward and speak to us, no matter when it happened.
"We know reporting allegations of this nature can be daunting, but specialist officers are on hand to provide support, answer questions and guide you through the process."
Allegations against the entertainer and children's author were published after he lost a legal bid to stop claims against him being made public by the media.
Some of the women in the investigation accused Walliams of "grooming" them when they were teenagers.
One now characterises her alleged encounter with Walliams at 15 years old as a "sexual assault". Walliams strongly denied he had any sexual contact with the girl.
He said he rejected any allegations of criminal activity and that he has never engaged in the grooming of young women.
The Guardian and ITV News said that several of the women, who do not know one another, allege they were targets of unwanted sexual advances from Walliams.
The investigation also claimed Walliams had a sexual relationship with at least one junior employee at publisher HarperCollins, and pursued another.
Other women alleged inappropriate behaviour at ITV's Britain's Got Talent, such as inviting girls and young women to his dressing room.

In a letter addressed to journalists working on the ITV and Guardian investigation, Walliams wrote: "Looking back, I realise that at times I behaved thoughtlessly towards other people I had casual sexual relationships with.
"I realise I did not always take people's feelings properly into account. That is something I regret.
"And whilst a power imbalance is inevitable when one party is famous, abusing that power is something else entirely and it is something that I never did."
He added: "I am not a sexual predator. I have not broken the law, but I am devastated that some of the women I met 10 to 20 years ago have now expressed hurt or anger towards me."
Walliams shot to fame in the early 2000s with BBC sketch comedy Little Britain, served as a judge on ITV's Britain's Got Talent and launched a best-selling series of children's books.

items.title: ‘Ahead of his time’: AI helps unlock discoveries hidden in notebooks of man who transformed maths
paragraphs: The Austrian logician Kurt Gödel was one of the most original thinkers of the 20th century. His two incompleteness theorems, published in 1931, transformed mathematics and paved the way for the digital age.
After his seminal results of the 1930s, Gödel published only a few papers. His unpublished work, however, runs to tens of thousands of pages, and is of great interest to historians of science.

Since 2017, the Finnish logician Jan von Plato has led a project at Helsinki University to understand the contents of 16 notebooks that Gödel wrote in the early 1940s. This material – the “workbooks” – is 1,009 pages of densely written text about maths and logic. Much of it is written in a German shorthand, Gabelsberger, that was obsolete even when Gödel was using it.

Progress in the mathematical understanding of the text was painfully slow – about a page a week – until September, when von Plato enlisted the help of the AI model Claude. Within a couple of days, Claude had provided a comprehensive digest of the entire material, revealing Gödel had proved hundreds of theorems that no one knew about.
The most famous logician of modern times had, in fact, discovered significantly more than anyone had thought.

“I was flabbergasted,” said von Plato. “The workbooks not only contain dozens of anticipations of results not known until the 70s and 80s, but they also contain 14 themes in logic that have not been pursued. Gödel was far ahead of his time.”

Gödel changed the course of logic because he revealed the limits of mathematical knowledge. His incompleteness theorems show that in all mathematical systems there are true statements that can neither be proved or disproved. Yet while this result was a blow to previous generations of logicians, who had hoped that all truths were verifiable, Gödel’s work pushed the field in new directions, inspiring Alan Turing to write his 1936 paper that began the theory of modern computation.

In 1940, Gödel fled Austria under the Nazis. He settled in Princeton, New Jersey, and became a close friend of Albert Einstein at the Institute of Advanced Study. Increasingly paranoid in his later years, he refused to eat food that was not cooked by his wife, and died of starvation in 1978.

Von Plato said he had started his Gödel project in 2017 because he was facing mandatory retirement from Helsinki University. “What should I do to make myself indispensable? Oh yes, I’ll start reading Gödel’s enigmatic shorthand pages!” He received a €2.5m (£2.1m) grant from the European Research Council, taught himself Gabelsberger shorthand – “I am one of only six people who can read it in the world” – and assembled a small team.

In August, at a conference in France about AI and theorem proving, von Plato met computer scientists who suggested that he co-opt the help of Claude in trying to make sense of the workbooks. On his return to Helsinki he began the process, showing Claude his transcriptions of the workbooks, as well as six books he had previously written on Gödel and other secondary scientific literature.

“In a couple of days, I got to see a 650-page explanation of the workbooks. It had to be controlled page for page, but it’s basically a work that is impossible to do for human beings,” he said. “Humans read one page at a time and we tend to forget things. It takes us a year to read about 50 pages. We just are not able to keep in mind all the different parts.
“The AI can connect all the pieces in a thousand pages. It can see all of Gödel’s writings as one piece.”

Gödel’s incompleteness theorems revealed the existence of statements whose truths were independent of the system they were written in: that is, they could not be proved or disproved within the system. In 1966, the American mathematician Paul Cohen won the Fields medal, the highest honour in maths, for showing the independence of two well-known mathematical statements: the continuum hypothesis and the axiom of choice.
Gödel reacted to Cohen’s Fields medal by saying that he had already proved the result in the 1940s. Yet when pushed for a proof by his peers, Gödel was unable to reconstruct one from his notes.

The first task von Plato set Claude was to discover if Gödel’s workbooks had a proof of the independence of the axiom of choice, which would reveal that Gödel had been telling the truth in 1966. The answer came back: yes, almost. “He was just one step away,” said von Plato. “There’s one definition that Gödel got wrong, but he had the right definition two years earlier, and so the thought is that he would have arrived at the right definition anyway if he had just continued for a few months. For me, the architecture of his proof is just wonderful. It makes all of these results of set theory follow a uniform pattern.

“What strikes me especially is that he starts from ideas. He’s not like someone who plays with formulas and hopes to arrive somewhere. He has very, very clear ideas, and then he’s methodical. Step after step he goes ahead and he manages to fulfil the aims that he has in this formal work.”

Von Plato said that when Claude presented him with the reconstructed proof of the independence of the axiom of choice, he ran it through the proof assistant Coq, a program that verifies the validity of mathematical proofs, and it passed. Von Plato believes that had Gödel published his work on the axiom of choice, he would have won the 1940 Fields medal. “Maybe he felt that when Cohen got the medal, that that was something he sort of missed.”

In further discussions with Claude, von Plato asked the AI model to extract all theorems in the workbooks for which Gödel either had a proof, had sketched a proof or had an idea for a proof. Claude found 663. When these results were put into Coq: “About 400 were verified as stated, about 200 were repaired, meaning that perhaps the statement of the theorem had to be made more precise, or some assumption had to be added. About 50 were false, and this is no wonder. Gödel himself, when rereading his notes, would occasionally add a marginal remark: falsch! [incorrect] or schlecht! [bad].”

Von Plato added: “I am sure that the continued study of Gödel’s manuscripts will reveal further treasures. The workbooks contain, Claude says, more than a dozen themes in logic and foundations of mathematics that have not been found in the 80-plus years since they were written down. So this is one thing to explore. But there are many others. His physics and cosmology notebooks are an unknown territory I plan to start exploring once I am finished with my present logic projects.”

Joel David Hamkins, a professor of logic at the University of Notre Dame, Indiana, has not seen Claude’s reconstruction of Gödel’s proof of the independence of the axiom of choice, but said that if it stood up “it is remarkable and historically interesting. Although how much is Claude and how much is Gödel is a job for the historians.”

Hamkins said: “The fact that there are things in there that resemble [Cohen’s proof] does not mean he had it. It shows he was on the path. You don’t get credit for work you don’t tell anyone about. But Gödel had so many ground-breaking ideas that it is maybe not surprising that his notebooks are full of exciting things.”

items.title: These IEMs get the Most Beautiful Earphones Award for 2026, but will their crowd-pleasing tuning win you over?
paragraphs: The ZiiGaat Seraphim IEMs stand out from the crowd because they just look so god damn beautiful. Luckily, their beauty's more than skin deep, and fans of rumbly sub-bass and an airy treble that brings detail to music without tiring your poor ears out will rejoice. But I can't help noticing that lean lower midrange which can take away some of the fullness of music that other IEMs at this price point keep.
Why you can trust Creative Bloq Our expert reviewers spend hours testing and comparing products and services so you can choose the best for you. Find out more about how we test.

I read recently that the Chi-fi space releases 200+ IEMs each year. It definitely feels like it, though when you disregard the crap and focus in on quality brands like ZiiGaat, Dunu, Kiwi Ears, Aful and Juzear, it's a far more manageable 100!

Price: $259 Release date: October 20265 drivers: 2DD + 3BAMaterial: CNC-machined aluminium shells, faceplates, and nozzlesCable: 1.2m modular (3.5mm & 4.4mm)Impedance: 9Ω @ 1kHzSensitivity: 125.5dB/Vrms @ 1kHzWeight: 5g each

Amongst the wave of IEMs to come out in 2026, I don't think I've been more excited about the look of an IEM than with the ZiiGaat Seraphim. And the more I found out about these beauties, the more excited I got about their sound.

Tuned by the consistently excellent Jay Audio, and combining two dynamic and three Knowles balanced armature drivers, the Seraphim promises a flagship-tier listening experience without – at $259 – the accompanying destruction to your wallet.

At this price point, they're not going to make my list of the best budget IEMs under $100, but there's every chance that they make my buying guide to the best IEMs under $500. Read on and see if they sound like the right option for you.

Overall sound: There was online chat about the Seraphim being a mini-Storm, but that's actually a bit of a red herring. I heard the Subtonic Storm at CanJam London, and from memory, it has much less emphasis on bass, noticeably fuller mids, and a significantly more nuanced, airy treble presentation overall. Instead, the Seraphim offers an exciting, contrasty sound with strong bass and a well-balanced treble. The mids are a little lean for me, and won't be for everyone, but if you're looking for sub-bass impact, these are your boyees!

Bass: The Seraphim uses an isobaric dual dynamic driver configuration that is meant to be good at delivering deep frequencies. I have no way of testing whether that's true, but what I can tell you is the sub-bass hits like a truck. In a good way.

Rather than bleeding into the lower midrange, the mid-bass remains tightly controlled, prioritising accuracy over bloated warmth. I really like this, as it provides a sense of bounce and grip texture, where bass guitar lines from Dry Cleaning's MySoul / Half Pint feel satisfying, while electronic kicks and 808s sound authoritative, separated, and just a blast to listen to.
However, this separation of upper bass and lower mids, while eliminating bleed, brings its own issues to the tuning...

For all my headphone and IEM reviews I play them through my Luxsin X8 and Chord Mojo 2 desktop DAC/Amps, as well as several dongles. This ensures sufficient power for peak performance, and provides a transparent source for a clean, detailed signal. My music sources are Spotify Lossless and CDs.

Midrange: Again, if marketing materials are to be believed (they're not, they're not!!) the Seraphim's Knowles balanced armatures allow the midrange to lean toward a clean, analytical profile that slightly favours upper registers.

For me, the midrange has pros and cons. Higher register vocals, such as Neil Young on Tell Me Why, are forward and engaging, cutting through the arrangement with transparency. But the lower mids feel a tad lean, stripping some natural body and chest resonance from vocals, especially on the lower tones of Barry White on Can't Get Enough of Your Love.

Despite this minor honkiness on certain vocal tracks, the instrument separation is really good, making every piano plonk and acoustic guitar strum sharply defined. I think the upper mids are so balanced that overall the timbre of the Seraphim is good, and instruments sound 'right', on the whole (though this is definitely where the Seraphim falls down against the CrinEar Reference – see the comparison section below for more on that).

Treble: The treble response is probably the most impressive part of the Seraphim's tuning. It delivers a highly resolving, crisp presentation without harsh peaks. It just seems to be very well balanced, offering a well-extended presentation, with just enough air to bring sparkle but without the tiring glare that you often get with bright IEMs.

I hear plenty of micro-details and coupled with the massive sub-bass, you could call this a very exciting V-shape tuning. Now, there's no perfect tuning, and especially when it comes to treble, one person's subtle spotlight is another's midday sun aimed at your eyeballs, and I think the Seraphim's treble can get a little much. But that's only on music that's mixed bright, like Michael Jackson's Billie Jean or Lucinda Williams's Sweet Old World.
But on 80% of my music library, the treble is smooth and fatigue-free, allowing for long listening sessions.
Price: At $259, the Seraphim sits in a competitive mid-fi price zone where consumers rightfully expect premium technicalities, durable accessories, and engaging tunings without glaring flaws.

And you get all of that with the Seraphim! It offers good detail retrieval, a thunderous sub-bass response, modular cable terminations, and a quality metal build that justifies its relatively modest asking price.
But how does it compare to the competition?

This is slightly unfair, as the Seraphim isn't going for the same style of tuning as the neutral Reference. Yet it's worth comparing, because at $350 the CrinEar Reference offers what I would describe as a far more sophisticated sound. There are lots of fun, exciting, contrasty, V-shaped IEMs out there, like the Seraphim. At the time of writing, there's only really one truly exceptional neutral IEM: The Reference.

When placing the Seraphim alongside the Reference, it's impossible to ignore the visual similarities. Aesthetically, the Seraphim is definitely trying to steal Crin’s lunch, mimicking the sleek metallic faceplates and minimalist shell contours. And Jay does it better! The Seraphim looks so much more engaging and visually interesting than the Reference's bland logo faceplate.

As mentioned, the sound is totally different. Where Crinacle goes for strict neutrality, emphasising natural vocal timbre and a smooth yet full midrange, the Seraphim leans heavily into a more flash, fun, V-shaped profile. It aggressively pushes that thunderous ten-decibel sub-bass slam and analytical treble, trading tonal purity for excitement and flair. And sometimes that's what I want! Most of the time, I get plenty excited by the balanced brilliance of the Reference.
Another area the Reference wins in is comfort. For me, the longer, deeper fit means a better seal is achieved quicker than with the Seraphim.

Pitting the Seraphim against the Binary EP321 is more of a fair fight. First of all, at $310 the Binary EP321 is more comparable price-wise. It's also a visually interesting IEM with its multi-coloured, reflective faceplate.

Sound-wise, it's a bright IEM with enough sub-bass and mid-bass to justify the 'exciting' descriptor. I think it does mid-bass better than the Seraphim, and with its extra treble, there's more detail in that bass with the EP321.

Most important for me, the EP321 is less lean in the lower mids, injecting much-needed warmth and thicker vocals that the Seraphim can lack. As mentioned, the Binary EP321 provides more treble energy thanks to its MEMS driver (says the marketing), meaning ultra-high frequencies are achieved with blinding speed.

Ultimately, if you crave physical sub-bass impact, grab the Seraphim, but if you prioritise airy treble and natural lower mids, the EP321 wins out easily. For me, I'd always go for the EP321 over the Seraphim.

ZiiGaat has fully embraced sturdy metal shells, providing an understated faceplate design that feels solid without being heavy. Although I've read online that some people don't like the thin cable, I'm a fan of it! After all, when was it decided that thick = great quality?! It wraps easily and avoids annoying microphonics entirely, which are major plusses for me.

In terms of ergonomics, the robust nozzles create a rather noticeably shallow fit, so I couldn't use my favourite Juzear eartips, as I wasn't able to get a proper seal, and instead I used the new rounder tips that came with the Dunu Vitruvian IEMs, which are longer. I still had issues with achieving a seal when swapping them with other IEMs for comparisons, but I don't expect many people will be doing that, and once I got the seal, it stayed, so I don't want to overstate it.

The Seraphim is mid-sized and I find them very comfortable when fitted. This makes them a good choice for long daily commutes or extended listening sessions at your desk without any noticeable fatigue.

I'm confident that the ZiiGaat Seraphim will be many people's idea of perfect in an IEM. Their tuning is ideal for audiophiles wanting visceral sub-bass impact combined with pristine detail retrieval. EDM fans and gamers will get on with them, with its punchy dynamics and superior imaging. They also look stand-out-beautiful, and though that's not enough by itself, it's a hell of a big plus in my book. After all, my favourite IEM is the CrinEar Reference, but I far prefer the look of the Seraphim!

Listeners seeking lush, thick male vocals should look elsewhere, as the lean lower mids will prove frustrating. However, despite a few subjective quirks, it remains an incredibly competent hybrid monitor, and I really liked it for the vast majority of my music library.

Beren cut his teeth as Staff Writer on digital art magazine ImagineFX, and has since worked on and edited several creative titles, including Paint & Draw and Computer Arts. As Ecom Editor on Creative Bloq, when he's not reviewing the latest audiophile headphones or evaluating the best designed ergonomic office chairs, he’s testing laptops, TVs and monitors, all so he can find the best tech deals for Creative Bloq’s digital professional audience.

items.title: Adobe's Black Friday deal is its biggest in years, with 57% off Creative Cloud Pro
paragraphs: The Adobe Black Friday sale has begun, and it was worth the wait if you've been holding out to lock in a year of savings on the world's most popular creative software. From today, you can save 57% on an annual Creative Cloud Pro subscription (new users only).

This is the biggest Adobe Black Friday deal we've seen for several years. You can get all of the Creative Cloud desktop apps, mobile apps and services for just $29.99 per month for a year in the US (down from $69.99). That includes Photoshop for digital art and image editing, Lightroom for photo editing, Premiere for video and Illustrator for vector art and graphic design. It's still the industry-standard package for professional creatives, and if you're in the US.

The Adobe Black Friday discount extends to the students and teachers plan, which is reduced by 77% to $15.99 for the first year. Pricing in other regions varies but often with similar discounts. Here are the details. In the UK, the price is reduced from £66.49 to £28.49 per month.

While there's a lot of competition in creative software today (see our guides to the best graphic design software and the best digital art software), we think Adobe's Creative Cloud still has the edge.

It's convenient to have a complete ecosystem of apps that integrate into multitool workflows, especially now that an increasing number of artists and designers are working across various media, from 2D design to motion graphics and video. Adobe also works continually on developing new tools and features to add to the suite, as we saw in the Adobe Sneaks 2026 presentation at the Adobe Max conference in Miami this past week. That means regular updates that add new tools, keeping the software ahead of the competition.

Joe is a regular freelance journalist and editor at Creative Bloq. He writes news, features and buying guides and keeps track of the best equipment and software for creatives, from video editing programs to monitors and accessories. A veteran news writer and photographer, he now works as a project manager at the London and Buenos Aires-based design, production and branding agency Hermana Creatives. There he manages a team of designers, photographers and video editors who specialise in producing visual content and design assets for the hospitality sector. He also dances Argentine tango.

items.title: First Ferrari Style flagship in New York features metallic facade
paragraphs: Architecture studios Formafantasma and Gonzalez Haase AAS have worked with Ferrari Style creative director Rocco Iannone on the brand’s first permanent store in New York, clad in a metallic facade.
Located in Manhattan’s SoHo neighbourhood, the flagship for Ferrari’s fashion label is in a long, narrow building at the corner of Prince Street and Mercer Street and spreads across two levels.
Berlin-based Gonzalez Haase AAS clad the building in brushed metal, with curved window mullions covering floor-to-ceiling glass along its length.

Under Iannone, the team referenced the Ferrari Officina concept, a central theme of the brand that seeks to connect fashion and automotive. It considers “the workshop as a junction at which artistic instinct, scientific rigour, craftsmanship and mechanical precision converge,” according to the team.
“The Officina is the place where intuition is given form through discipline, and where the human touch works in harmony with mechanical precision,” said Iannone.
The opening follows another Ferrari Style store opened earlier this year in London, designed by the same team, and both stores share pops of red, warm beige finishes, and steel accents.
However, the New York space was designed to fit in with the city. The team said the New York location reflects the “form, scale and material character of SoHo”.

“For New York, we wanted to translate this spirit into a space in which architecture, fashion and object design each retain their own identity while contributing to a single Ferrari language,” said the team.
“Every material and detail has been chosen to express this balance between art and science, creating an environment that is open, evolving and in direct dialogue with the energy of SoHo.”
Men’s ready-to-wear is located on the first floor, with objects displayed on units designed by Formafantasma.
The space is bordered by a deep red curtain and large rectangular ceiling lights.
A staircase to the left side of the store leads to the “more intimate” second level, containing women’s ready-to-wear, footwear and accessories collections.
It also contains the store’s atelier, the second worldwide apart from the London location.
Wrapped in leather curtains, the space provides a private setting for personalisations and alterations. A table containing samples of textiles and hardware sits at the centre.
Ferrari Style, the brand’s luxury fashion line founded in 2021, has other US locations in New Jersey, Miami, and Las Vegas.
Ferrari recently unveiled a laptop collaboration with HP, as well as its first electric vehicle earlier this year.

items.title: Bessent blames Lutnick's Commerce Department for failing to block Megaspeed
paragraphs: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has blamed the Commerce Department, run by Howard Lutnick, of failing to properly oversee the export of high-specification Nvidia chips, as the fallout from the scandal widens.
Jensen Huang left the company he co-founded after revelations he had an affair a former Megaspeed executive. The firm had been buying advanced chips from Nvidia.

Megaspeed had been probed by US government agencies over suspicions it had been smuggling those chips into China, reports said, but it is not on a list of firms that US companies are prevented from working with.
Bessent told CNBC several government agencies "were in favour of putting Megaspeed on the entity list for months".
"But Commerce has the pen... and you will have to ask them about their internal process," he added.
Bessent also said he was "frustrated" by delays in putting the company on the export control list and reports of leakage of AI chips into China.

"President Trump made it very clear that China should not receive any Nvidia chips above H100s, so any leakage is very frustrating because it hurts our great companies in the AI race, because it gives the Chinese an advantage," he said.
Last year, the Commerce Department had been investigating Megaspeed over suspicions it had been smuggling some of Nvidia's advanced AI chips into China, according to the New York Times.

There was also pressure on the Commerce Department to add it to the list, but separate reporting in the Financial Times said the department was delaying efforts to have the cloud computing firm included.
However, Bessent also pointed the finger at Nvidia.
"The story has been thus far of Jensen Huang's personal foibles," he told CNBC's Squawk Box programme, external.

"The real story here should be: Did Nvidia know their client, and was there a robust effort at Nvidia to make sure that there was no leakage and that they were selling to what were obviously pass-through shell companies?
"It's important that anyone at the company there be held accountable for that."
Megaspeed has been contacted for comment.

items.title: Climate action discussed at youth COP meeting
paragraphs: School children are taking part in an event aimed at inspiring climate action, to coincide with the COP31 international climate conference in Turkey.
Hosted at the Kingston Maurwood campus, the first Dorset-wide Youth COP has brought children from 14 schools together to discuss issues including future careers.
Maria Clarke, of Dorset Local Nature Partnership, said young people should be "given a voice" over dealing with climate change.
A Dorset COP 2026 event is also being held on Saturday as world leaders and delegates gather at Antalya in Turkey for the COP31 climate summit.

The Dorset Youth COP event includes discussions about how young people feel about climate change as well as a panel session introducing them to the range of jobs and careers in the climate and energy sectors.

Maria Clarke, of Dorset Local Nature Partnership, said: "Young people are inheriting the climate and ecological emergencies that previous generations have created and need to be given a voice in jointly developing and implementing the solutions to these issues."
"The Youth COP aims to raise awareness, inspire and support them to take action now and into the future."

items.title: 'Hardest challenge of my life' - Owain Wyn Evans completes Children in Need ride
paragraphs: Presenter Owain Wyn Evans has completed his challenge of cycling through all four UK nations to raise money for BBC Children in Need.
The Welsh host of BBC Radio 2's Early Breakfast Show rode almost 400 miles, setting off from Glasgow and finishing in Cardiff on Friday.
The challenge started on 9 November in Scotland and over the next five days, Owain rode through Northern Ireland, England and Wales and raised £3,853,530 in the process.
Reflecting on his journey, he said: "This has been the hardest challenge of my life, 100%.
"I can't believe I'm here. It's overwhelming, all the love and passion and commitment people have shown."
The BBC said Owain's challenge would be the "greatest-ever distance" covered in a Radio 2 endeavour for the charity.
He crossed the finish line in Cardiff's Central Square just after 11:00 GMT, and was greeted by a crowd cheering him on before he was met by his husband, Arran Rees.
Owain, 42, whose bike was named Shania Chain, and decked out in Children in Need colours - Pudsey's favourite yellow with coloured spots - said: "Thank you so much everyone, from me and Shania.
"Honestly, this has felt so far away for such a long time. I can't believe that I'm here with this welcome and the sun's out."
Hollywood actor Luke Evans announced the route to Owain each day on BBC Radio 2.
During the 640km feat, he was also surprised with the premiere of Steps' brand-new version of their debut hit 5, 6, 7, 8, retitled 5, 6, 7, donate, which featured new lyrics and extra vocals.
It was recorded to help boost Owain's spirits on the longest day of his challenge.
The broadcaster also expressed his gratitude for the support of Radio 2 listeners.

His messages of support from public figures included one from the Princess of Wales, who recorded a message for him in Welsh, saying: "Hi Owain, it's Catherine, you're doing so well. Keep going. Wishing you all the very best."
Shania Twain was so impressed that the bike had been named after her that she sent a message of good luck before the challenge.
She said: "Hi Owain, Shania Twain here. You're about to take on an incredible challenge for BBC Children in Need, cycling 400 miles through all four nations.
"As you set off in Glasgow, I just want to say: 'Let's Go, Owain!' We'll be cheering you on all the way. Good luck."
She sent him another message when he finished, saying: "Congratulations on completing your incredible challenge for Children in Need. You're still the one my friend, sending you all my love."
Helen Thomas, head of Radio 2, said: "Owain truly captured the hearts of the nation this week as he battled through his epic four nations Challenge.
"On behalf of all the Radio 2 listeners as well as the thousands of children and families who will benefit from his Herculean fundraising efforts we simply can't thank him enough. Diolch Owain! "

items.title: Kisses galore, seaside shenigans, McRoman adventures and street feats – the week in art
paragraphs: Nicole Eisenman A free display beside the seaside from the witty and imaginative sort-of-figurative artist. Turner Contemporary, Margate, from 14 November to 11 April
The Last Human Kiss Snogging galore by Wolfgang Tillmans, Tracey Emin and other contemporary romantics. Sainsbury Centre, Norwich, until 11 April

Roman Scotland Images of classical gods, tombs of fallen legionaries and mysterious relics of Pictish life in a journey to the edge of the Roman empire and beyond. National Museum of Scotland, Edinburgh, from 14 November to 18 April

Beyond the Streets In spite of the title, this is very much a celebration of street art and culture starring Shepard Fairey, Goldie, Jenny Holzer and many, many more. Saatchi Gallery, London, until 5 May
Dialogues: Wilhelmina Barns-Graham x Haroun Hayward A contemporary artist goes head-to-head with the noted modernist who died in 2004. Hales Gallery, London, until 18 December

We found Tate Britain’s new exhibition, Vanessa Bell & Duncan Grant: Inside Bloomsbury, an “epic yet flaccid roam through the complicated lives and desperately mediocre paintings” of the co-habiting modernists. Read the full review
The brilliantly bolshie artist Ryan Gander lambasted practically everyone
Jill Posener’s cheeky, feminist photography served as a rebuttal to 80s misogyny
Epstein survivors were overwhelmed by messages of support at pop-up art exhibition
The Vatican houses a collection of Indigenous treasures questionably ‘gifted’ to it
Head of Christ Crucified by the Master of Liesborn (Johann von Soest?), probably early 1480s-1490

The blood streams over Christ’s deathly white face in a vivid, almost Hammer horror contrast between gore and pallor. It flows in thick rivulets from the crown of thorns that has been mockingly forced on to his head. The initials INRI on a piece of paper fixed to the cross stand for “Jesus of Nazareth, King of the Jews” in Latin, and the cruel crown rams home the barb. Christ bears the laughter and the physical pain with patience and dignity, lowering his eyes in sorrow as he waits for his earthly body to die. The stark, simple shock of this image comes from an age in which Europeans were encouraged to identify with Christ, to imagine themselves suffering alongside him. At the same time this artist’s explicit focus on flowing blood may serve a theological function: the central moment of the medieval Mass was the miraculous transformation of bread and wine into the actual body and blood of Christ. According to the philosopher Thomas Aquinas this took place literally: the bread and wine kept their “accidental” appearance while changing their “essential” nature. This painting is part of an altarpiece from Germany, but not all Germans were convinced by such ideas. In the early 1500s Martin Luther would rebel against the miracle of transubstantiation, and against art like this which he regarded as idolatry. National Gallery, London

items.title: Political divide threatens Kurdish autonomy; US urges unity
paragraphs: Editor's note: this story was translated from the original VOA Kurdish article.
Last week's withdrawal of the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan from the Iraqi Kurdistan’s regional government has deepened the political standoff between the region's two main ruling parties.
The rise in tensions came after a disputed parliamentary session prompted the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK) to announce its withdrawal from the Kurdistan Regional Government (KRG).

The Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP), led by the Barzani family, and the PUK, led by the Talabani family, have dominated Kurdish politics for decades. Their rivalry led to a brutal armed conflict and separate administrations in the 1990s.
Some regional analysts warn that the latest tensions could lead to a renewed division of the Kurdistan region.

"If we divide this region ourselves, the entire world will abandon us,” Kamil Omar, a university professor in Sulaimaniyah, told VOA. “How long can they continue worrying about us when we cannot protect our own region, our people’s future and our nation’s strategic interests?”
The Kurdistan Region gained de facto autonomy following the 1991 Gulf War, with its federal status recognized in Iraq’s 2005 constitution.
“We have received political and military support and protection from international allies for the past 35 years," he added.

Speaking at Chatham House in London on Wednesday, U.S. special envoy for Syria and Iraq Tom Barrack urged Kurdish leaders to overcome their “family” and “tribal” divisions and strengthen cooperation with Baghdad.
“This is an Iraqi issue. This is an Iraqi decision. This is not an American decision,” Barrack said. “My advice, the president’s advice, is: Get over it.”
Masoud Haider, a KDP member and former Iraqi deputy finance minister, described Barrack’s remarks as a clear political message urging both parties to agree on forming a government.

“A strong Kurdistan Region with unified institutions contributes to Iraq’s strength and stability,” Haider told VOA. “This message calls on Kurdish political forces to put their differences aside and form a government based on cooperation and responsibility.”
Mahmoud Khoshnaw, a PUK member, described Barrack’s remarks as both a reflection of political realities and a warning.

“Any step that promotes stability and development strengthens the region, while any step that undermines stability, creates political divisions or marginalizes a political party weakens it,” Khoshnaw told VOA.
Speaking Thursday at the Sulaimani Forum, PUK leader Bafel Talabani described the dispute as “the single largest political crisis in the history of the Kurdistan Region.”
He rejected the legitimacy of the disputed parliamentary process and warned against further unilateral moves.
“We effectively have two administrations,” Talabani said, although he cautioned that discussing two separate governments was premature.
“Every escalation will be met with a well-planned escalation,” he warned, adding that dialogue remained possible.
Talabani rejected characterizing the dispute as a family feud, describing it instead as a longstanding rivalry between two political forces.
On Monday, KDP leader Masoud Barzani called for negotiations.
“I call on our brothers in the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan to sit down with the KDP, resolve the problems and bring an end to the Kurdistan Region’s political crisis,” Barzani said in a statement.
The KRG Council of Ministers, meeting Wednesday without PUK ministers, also urged them to return and address their concerns through cabinet discussions.
Talabani dismissed those appeals as political rhetoric intended to shift blame for the divisions onto the PUK.

items.title: What we know about the global outage
paragraphs: More than 430 million people use Microsoft 365 apps according to Microsoft's website.
The full scale of the outage has not been confirmed, but monitoring website Downdetector had 140,000 people from 74 countries report issues with Outlook on Thursday evening.
The real figure affected is likely much higher because Downdetector relies primarily on users self-reporting.
Microsoft 365 is also used by companies worldwide and is expected to have a knock-on effect to other services.
Tech giants OpenAI and Anthropic have both reported problems as a result of the outage.
ChatGPT-maker OpenAI said it was investigating an issue affecting its connections to Microsoft's services, which has caused some tools to not work as expected.
From city governments in the US to Australian spy agencies, disruption across the globe has been widespread.
Courts from Los Angeles to Texas warned that communications might be delayed.
In Canada, the public broadcaster CBC reported that a healthcare network running several hospitals in Toronto was experiencing email issues, but that patient care was not affected.
The government of Japan also said its shared IT platform had been disrupted.
Across the UK, GP surgeries, pharmacies, police and schools have been affected by the outage.

Some GP surgeries have urged patients not to submit messages via their website while the problem remains, while several large police forces are urging members of the public to call if they want to make a report.
Although email service Outlook appears to be resuming for some, the outage has so far lasted for more than 20 hours - in outage terms that is considered a long time.
Prof James Ferryman from the University of Reading's department of computer science said the details the company has disclosed provide some clues.
"What Microsoft has told us is that the part of its servers that sets up secure connections is getting swamped, and once that happens the server just stops answering," he said.
"The trouble is that this kind of failure snowballs.
"One server falls over, its work gets passed to the next one, and meanwhile huge numbers of phones and laptops keep trying to get back in.
"You can't just turn it all back on at once. You have to bring it back bit by bit."
The challenge is therefore not just fixing the fault, but managing the huge surge of devices trying to reconnect once services start coming back online.
Gergely Orosz, a former leading software engineer at several major tech companies including Skype and Uber, said this could be the "most disruptive" business email outage "of all time".
He said it was still difficult to know just how many people have been affected by the disruption, but added he "cannot recall" an outage over business email ever taking this long to return to normal.
Australian cyber-security expert Troy Hunt told the BBC the outage could have far-reaching consequences.
"Microsoft is a massive part of the internet backbone and reminds us how critical email still is.

"Not only does this outage affect many people's ability to work but also things like the ability to communicate about appointments, purchase things that need verification, create or access accounts and services," he said.

items.title: Marlon Brando cool to Jensen Huang joke: how the black leather jacket became a meme
paragraphs: For nearly two decades a black leather jacket has been a key part of Jensen Huang’s look. Now it has become a punchline.

As the founder and chief executive of Nvidia resigned this week after reports of multiple affairs, his affinity for a leather jacket, an item of clothing typically associated with a man in midlife crisis mode, has become widely mocked.

The Cut ran a story suggesting a clear line between his penchant for a luxury leather jacket and his extramarital affairs. “Jensen Huang’s leather jackets confessed before he did” read the headline. Writing in the New York Times, the author Anand Giridharadas asked “is an expensive leather jacket on a middle-aged man the new symbol of a honeypot victim?”

Meanwhile, the internet is rife with memes, including an AI-generated image of a leather jacket flying at half mast outside Elon Musk’s rocket company SpaceX. There was also another fake image, this time of Huang in a studded leather jacket, that many people believed was real.

Elsewhere, there are plenty of divorced dad jokes doing the rounds. “Jensen leather jacket discourse reminds me of the time two years ago when I wore my beloved moto jacket to a party and my good friend said “great jacket, sorry you got divorced”, wrote one user on X.

Similar to Steve Jobs’s black rollneck and jeans or Mark Zuckerberg’s Latin-sloganed T-shirts, Huang’s black leather jacket has become a visual trademark. He likes to pair a leather jacket (always black) with a black T-shirt and black jeans.

In September, in an interview with CBS, Huang explained he had 30 to 40 leather jackets. He credited his wife, Lori Huang, with choosing them. They vary from motorcycle-inspired jackets with a tighter fit and plenty of zips to collarless croc-embossed jackets and clean-cut tailored versions. He has worn them to trade shows, to parties and to give keynote speeches at developer conferences. In 2021 he appeared on the cover of Time magazine in a black leather jacket from Tom Ford. In July, another Tom Ford jacket worn and signed by Huang sold at a charity auction at Sotheby’s for $960,000, more than 10 times its original price.
“The leather jacket is Huang’s way of borrowing some cool,” says Peter Bevan, a writer and stylist. Bevan points to the leather jacket’s “rebel history” as part of the appeal.

Marlon Brando led his biker gang wearing an asymmetric zip jacket in 1953’s The Wild One; James Dean zipped around off-screen in a similar style while following his Berlin era; David Bowie wore a black leather jacket on the cover of his Heroes album in 1977. Patrick Swayze in Dirty Dancing, John Travolta in Grease and Harrison Ford as Indiana Jones also made a leather jacket an enduring symbol of Hollywood style.
By choosing a black leather jacket rather than a corporate suit, it suggests that Huang is unconventional, a leader rather than a conformist.
“It’s basically Huang saying: ‘I’m not a regular billionaire boss, I’m a cool billionaire boss’,” Bevan says.

When asked by CBS in October why he wore a leather jacket day in, and day out, Huang said it helped him avoid decision fatigue. “Black is the absence of choice,” he said. “It’s nice to wear the same thing every day because no surprises. For everybody else, they probably have to make three or four decisions. I took that off my plate. The moment I wake up, I could be thinking about important things.”

It’s a look that has not gone unnoticed by his fellow tech giants. In 2024, Zuckerberg posted a photo of Huang swapping jackets. Later in the year, at a Siggraph conference in Colorado, Zuckerberg presented him with another jacket. “It’s black and leather and shearling,” Zuckerberg said describing the coat. “It’s a vibe. I mean, get this guy a chain.” In return, Huang gave him the black leather jacket he was wearing, explaining that Lori had bought it for him to commemorate that year’s conference. “This is worth more because it’s used,” Zuckerberg said as he slipped it on.

Bevan says that while Huang’s choice of designer jackets are “the kind that most fashion insiders would rate”, a box-fresh leather jacket “feels try hard” and as a result, “tips into midlife crisis territory fast”.
The biggest mistake men make when buying a leather jacket Bevan says is choosing one that is “too shiny, too new and too tight.”
The list of those who get it wrong is long – including Jeremy Clarkson, who likes to wear a black leather jacket with bootcut jeans.
For Bevan, the men who have mastered a leather jacket are those who “look like they’ve owned it for ever”.

Lenny Kravitz who, like Huang, is in his 60s, prefers a battered leather jacket. John Malkovich, who is a decade older, likes a brown oversized leather jacket, while the rapper A$AP Rocky, who is in his 30s, has made a bomber leather jacket his style staple.

For those without youth or “rock-star DNA” on their side, Bevan suggests ditching a leather jacket for a cotton Harrington style that he describes as “having the same cool but none of the leather-clad midlife baggage”.

As for Huang, he may have to reconsider his default wardrobe for next week. While he managed to pull off a leather jacket at tech conferences, it may be harder to pull off at a congressional testimony.

items.title: Russia is ‘setting traps’ in Ukraine talks, EU foreign policy chief warns
paragraphs: The EU’s foreign policy chief has warned against “walking into the traps that Russia is setting” as she said Moscow was trying to start a debate about European security in order to divert attention from its aggression.

“We have one aggressor and one victim, and the aggressor does not have security concerns,” Kaja Kallas said on arrival at an EU leaders’ summit in Dublin. “Nobody has ever attacked them. They have attacked others. I mean, keep the focus, people.”

In talks on the Ukraine war, Russia has revived its hardline demands for a total overhaul of European security – demands that were rejected in 2021 because they were seen as an infringement of the sovereignty of central and eastern European countries. The latest round of talks between Ukraine, Russia and the US were held this week in Abu Dhabi.

Donald Trump’s envoy and son-in-law, Jared Kushner, said on Thursday night that Russia and Ukraine had agreed to expand the next round of peace negotiations to include the Europeans. However, Russia quickly contradicted that assurance.

European leaders have long said they will support Ukraine in any peace talks, but want to see a ceasefire before negotiations. They also stress the continent has an extensive web of security agreements that Russia has violated.

Friedrich Merz, the German chancellor, said: “Russia wants to talk about questions of a European security architecture. We do not need to discuss that; it already exists.” He added that it was a “given” that his country would be part of any European delegation.
The European Commission president, Ursula von der Leyen, said it was “self-explanatory that Europe is included in the peace talks to safeguard our interests, but also to support Ukraine”.

The Kremlin said on Friday: “Once we understand [Europe’s] real intentions and their willingness to contribute to the peace process, then we can make a decision on holding talks in an expanded format.” Russia’s lead negotiator in Abu Dhabi, Vladimir Medinsky, said it was “unclear what there is to discuss” with Europe.
The US call to involve Europe in talks has turned the spotlight on who would represent it.

Despite more than two years of on-off talks, the EU has not settled on a choice. But there is a growing view that Europe should not be represented by a single person, but by different interlocutors from the wider continent.

Paris and Berlin support a continued role for their own envoys in the E3 format of Britain, France and Germany, alongside EU representatives. Smaller member states put the emphasis more firmly on the EU representatives: the European Council’s president, António Costa, and Kallas, the EU’s high representative for foreign affairs and security policy.
Sweden’s prime minister, Ulf Kristersson, said the discussion on who should represent Europe was “slightly overstated” as it had differing interests.

Some of the issues in peace talks were “pure EU interests”, he said, citing financing Kyiv and Ukraine’s future membership in the bloc. He also supported other formats, such as the “pretty uncomplicated” E3 and the “very legitimate” E5, which includes Italy and Poland, as well as a role for EU representatives. He said: “I am quite flexible on that. I think what we actually say is more important than the exact configuration of the people in the room.”

Several at the summit, including Kallas, also pointed to the importance of including the UK, a founder member of the coalition of the willing, a broad group of countries committed to future peacekeeping in Ukraine.
Ireland’s taoiseach, Micheál Martin, said the UK and Norway each had a significant role and “that all has to be taken into consideration because it’s a European, continent-wide issue”.

The British prime minister, Andy Burnham, said it was for the EU to decide who would represent the bloc. He said there was a strong view among European leaders that it was for Europe – in the wider sense – “to decide its own arrangements” on security.

items.title: Trump loses control of Congress – level 1
paragraphs: The Democrats win a big election in the US. They now control Congress. President Donald Trump and his team lose many votes.

Now, people in both political parties are fighting about what to do next. Vice President JD Vance says that the war with Iran is a bad idea. Many people do not like Trump anymore because of that. Trump said that his immigration rules are too hard. But he still puts his immigration leader in a top job. At the same time, Democrats are trying to agree on new plans for the country.
Experts think that it will still be very hard for leaders in Washington to pass new laws and help people quickly.

Difficult words: vote (when a person formally chooses a person in an election), immigration rules (what people who come from other countries must and must not do), pass (to officially say yes to a new rule).
You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

items.title: Trump loses control of Congress – level 2
paragraphs: The Democratic Party won big in the US midterm elections and took control of both houses of Congress from President Donald Trump’s Republican Party.

This defeat caused strong arguments inside both parties. Vice President JD Vance blamed the election loss on the war with Iran, and disagreed directly with Trump. At the same time, Trump said his strict immigration rules went too far, but he still chose the creator of those rules to lead his White House team. Meanwhile, Democrats are fighting over their plans, as its members want different things.

Experts say that even with new Democratic leaders in Congress, it will be hard to pass major new laws because the president can still block them, which may lead to more political delays in Washington.

Difficult words: defeat (the loss of a contest, game, election, or battle), blame (to say or think that someone or something is responsible for something bad that happened), major (important, big, serious).
You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

items.title: Trump loses control of Congress – level 3
paragraphs: Following a decisive defeat in the US midterm elections, Donald Trump and the Republican Party have lost control of both houses of Congress to the Democrats. The results have sparked intense disputes within both major parties.

Among Republicans, Vice President JD Vance has attributed the electoral losses to the unpopular war with Iran, which created a visible rift with the president. At the same time, Donald Trump has sent mixed signals regarding his policy direction: while publicly acknowledging that his strict immigration enforcement went too far, he appointed Stephen Miller, the architect of those policies, as White House Chief of Staff. On the Democratic side, progressives and moderates are competing to shape the party’s future legislative agenda.

Political analysts warn that despite the significant shift in congressional control, deep ideological divisions and the president’s veto power will likely lead to continued political gridlock in Washington rather than major policy changes.

Difficult words: dispute (a disagreement, argument, or debate between people, parties, or groups), rift (a serious break in friendly relations between people or groups), gridlock (a situation where no progress can be made because of strong disagreement or opposing forces).
